tools.name: get_campaign_attribution_reports
tools.description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "get_campaign_attribution_reports" and follow it. The dimension names, filter syntax, date-range semantics, grouping rules, and query patterns live in tool_guidance, not in this description; calling this tool without them produces wrong or failed queries. If you skip tool_guidance, submit your first call with hasReadToolInstructions=false (the default); the tool will return status=READ_TOOL_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED with the full instructions in toolInstructions — read them, then retry with hasReadToolInstructions=true. Revenue ranking: dimensions=[CAMPAIGN], metrics=[REVENUE], sortByMetric=REVENUE. Attribution data tool: all metrics (revenue, deal amounts, deal counts, contact counts) are scoped to the closed-won deal attribution pipeline. Use for revenue, attributed deal, and attributed contact questions. CONTACT_COUNT = contacts whose interactions influenced closed-won deals; this is NOT a "new contacts generated" metric. For non-attribution contact queries (new contacts, influenced contacts, sessions), use read_campaign_data with GET_ANALYTICS. TOP/BEST PERFORMING ASSET: use dimension=ASSET_TITLE; set sortByMetric to the metric the question asks about (REVENUE when unspecified, DEAL_COUNT for "most deals", DEAL_AMOUNT for "highest deal value", CONTACT_COUNT for "most contacts", ATTRIBUTION_COUNT for "most interactions"). Attribution metrics share a common unit across all asset types. Do NOT rank by calling getCampaignAssetMetrics per type — those engagement metrics (views vs. open rate) are not cross-type comparable. Scope note: this data covers closed-won / attributed deals only. For deals at any stage (open, opportunity, qualifiedtobuy, and so on), use read_campaign_data with operation=GET_ASSET_METRICS and assetType=DEAL (returns name, stage, amount, close date for all associated deals). search_crm_objects is less reliable, use only if that fails. For long-running queries, this returns a PROCESSING status with a taskId to poll for results.

taskId.description: Poll for results of a previously submitted query. Pass the taskId from a PROCESSING response.

mode.description: Report mode. Only AGGREGATION is currently supported.

dimensions.description: How to group data (AGGREGATION mode). Max 2 per query. Omit for ungrouped totals. Key mappings: 'channels' or 'content types' (emails, ads, landing pages) -> ASSET_TYPE; specific asset names -> ASSET_TITLE; 'influence types' or 'engagement types' -> INTERACTION_TYPE; traffic/referral source -> INTERACTION_SOURCE; deal names -> DEAL_NAME; deal IDs (for links) -> DEAL.

metrics.description: Required: What to measure. REVENUE for attributed revenue (use for any non-deal breakdown like channel/source/asset), DEAL_AMOUNT for per-deal or total deal value (always grouped by deal), DEAL_COUNT for unique deals, CONTACT_COUNT for unique contacts, ATTRIBUTION_COUNT for touchpoint volume.

attributionModel.description: Revenue attribution model for the REVENUE metric. Defaults to LINEAR. See instructions for valid values.

campaignCrmObjectIds.description: Campaign CRM object IDs to scope the query. Empty for cross-campaign analysis.

startDate.description: Start of date range filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Must pair with endDate or both omitted. Filters by deal close date for REVENUE/DEAL_AMOUNT, deal create date for DEAL_COUNT, touchpoint timestamp for CONTACT_COUNT/ATTRIBUTION_COUNT.

endDate.description: End of date range filter (YYYY-MM-DD). Must pair with startDate or both omitted.

dimension.description: Dimension to filter on (e.g. ASSET_TYPE, INTERACTION_POSITION). Uses the same names as dimensions.

operator.description: Filter operator: EQ, NEQ, IN, NOT_IN, GT, GTE, LT, LTE, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY.

value.description: Single value for EQ, NEQ, GT, GTE, LT, LTE operators.

values.description: Multiple values for IN, NOT_IN operators.

filters.description: Server-side filters on any dimension property. See instructions for examples.

sortByMetric.description: Sort results by this metric (DESC by default). Use to rank rows without post-processing, e.g. REVENUE returns highest-revenue rows first.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction for sortByMetric. ASC or DESC. Defaults to DESC.

limit.description: Max result rows returned by the server. Defaults to 100, maximum 500. When responseFormat=CONCISE, zero-value rows are filtered client-side after the server applies this limit, so fewer rows than requested may be returned.

responseFormat.description: Controls response verbosity. CONCISE (default) omits zero-value metric entries and drops rows where all metrics are zero, reducing token usage by up to ~⅔. DETAILED returns all rows and fields including zero values.

hasReadToolInstructions.description: Set to true once you have read the instructions for get_campaign_attribution_reports — either via tool_guidance (preferred) or from a READ_TOOL_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED response. IMPORTANT: after calling tool_guidance for this tool, your very next call to get_campaign_attribution_reports MUST include hasReadToolInstructions=true. Omitting it (default false) triggers an inline READ_TOOL_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED response instead of executing the query; do not omit it once you have already read the instructions from tool_guidance. Not required when polling with taskId.

tools.name: manage_campaign_objects
tools.description:
REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "manage_campaign_objects".
Creates or updates campaigns, assigns campaign owners, and manages asset associations.

<prerequisites>
Use CRM tools to retrieve the campaign's campaignCrmObjectId before using CAMPAIGN_UPDATE or CAMPAIGN_ASSET operations.
</prerequisites>

<mandatory_confirmation_process>
Always show proposed changes in a table and get explicit user approval before creating or updating campaigns or modifying asset associations. This step is CRITICAL.

  <confirmation_rules>
  - **First confirmation only**: Add this line after the approval prompt: "Want to skip confirmations for this chat? Just ask."
  - **After 1 confirmation**: Stop offering the skip option, but keep confirming
  - **If user opts out**: Skip confirmations for remainder of session
  </confirmation_rules>

  <confirmation_format>
  Proposed Changes:

  | operationType   | Field       | Value             |
  |-----------------|-------------|-------------------|
  | CAMPAIGN_CREATE | displayName | Q3 Brand Campaign |

  Approve? [✅ Yes / ❌ No]
  Want to skip confirmations for this chat? Just ask.
  </confirmation_format>
</mandatory_confirmation_process>

<operations>
The `operationType` field is required on every request:
- CAMPAIGN_CREATE: set `createRequest` with required `displayName`, optional `startDate`, `endDate`, `goal`, `audience`, `notes`, `customProperties`.
- CAMPAIGN_UPDATE: set `updateRequest` with required `campaignCrmObjectId`, optional `displayName`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `goal`, `audience`, `notes`, `customProperties`.
- CAMPAIGN_ASSET: set `assetRequest` with required `campaignCrmObjectId`, `assetOperations` (non-empty list of `{action, assetObjectType, crmObjectIds}`). Each entry has its own ADD|REMOVE action. Check `assetOperationFailures` in the response — if non-empty, those operations failed; succeeded ones are already applied. Call CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES_LIST first.
- CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES_LIST: no additional fields required.
</operations>

displayName.description: Required. The campaign display name (max 255 chars).

startDate.description: Campaign start date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description: Campaign end date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

owner.description: Campaign CRM owner ID, not a HubSpot user ID. Look it up with CRM owner tools.

colorHex.description: Campaign color as a hex string in the format #RRGGBB (for example #FF5733).

status.description: Campaign status (sets hs_campaign_status). One of: planned, in_progress, active, paused, completed.

customProperties.description: Custom campaign properties as a map of property name to value. To set the campaign status or color, use the status or colorHex fields instead of hs_campaign_status or hs_color_hex.

createRequest.description: Campaign creation data. Required when operationType is CAMPAIGN_CREATE.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: Required. CRM object ID of the campaign to update. If you only have the campaign name, look it up first via CRM search or read_campaign_data; do not guess it.

startDate.description: Campaign start date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description: Campaign end date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

owner.description: Campaign CRM owner ID, not a HubSpot user ID. Look it up with CRM owner tools.

colorHex.description: Campaign color as a hex string in the format #RRGGBB (for example #FF5733).

status.description: Campaign status (sets hs_campaign_status). One of: planned, in_progress, active, paused, completed.

customProperties.description: Custom campaign properties as a map of property name to value. To set the campaign status or color, use the status or colorHex fields instead of hs_campaign_status or hs_color_hex.

updateRequest.description: Campaign update data. Required when operationType is CAMPAIGN_UPDATE.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: Required. CRM object ID of the campaign. If you only have the campaign name, look it up first via CRM search or read_campaign_data; do not guess it.

action.description: Required. The action to perform for this asset type: ADD or REMOVE.

assetObjectType.description: Required. The asset object type name (e.g. LANDING_PAGE, BLOG_POST, SITE_PAGE, MARKETING_EMAIL).

crmObjectIds.description: Required. CRM object IDs of the assets to associate or dissociate.

assetOperations.description: Required. One or more asset type operations. Each entry specifies an action (ADD|REMOVE), assetObjectType, and crmObjectIds, allowing ADD and REMOVE to be mixed in a single call. Each (action, assetObjectType) pair must appear at most once — e.g. ADD+LANDING_PAGE and REMOVE+LANDING_PAGE can coexist, but two ADD+LANDING_PAGE entries cannot. Operations are applied sequentially — if one fails, prior operations are not rolled back. Call CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES_LIST to discover valid assetObjectType values.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description:
Collects and submits user feedback about the HubSpot connector to HubSpot. Only after the user explicitly confirms the exact feedback to send.

<scope>
EXCLUSIVELY for feedback about HubSpot connector tools (search_crm_objects, manage_crm_objects, get_properties, etc.). Do NOT use for:
- Non-HubSpot tools (Slack, Microsoft 365, Notion, iMessage, Intercom, etc.)
- General AI/LLM quality (wrong answers, hallucinations, formatting)
- HubSpot product/UI issues unrelated to the connector
If the issue is not about a HubSpot connector tool, do NOT initiate feedback - tell the user this channel is for HubSpot connector issues only.
</scope>

<when_to_invoke>
Agent-detected: user corrects HubSpot connector behavior, reports it returned wrong data/errors, or is dissatisfied with a HubSpot connector tool.
User-initiated: explicit requests ("I want to give feedback"), or intent to reach HubSpot ("HubSpot should know...", "Tell HubSpot...").
</when_to_invoke>

<flow>
1. Agent-detected only: finish your answer first, then after a divider (---) note the connector issue and OFFER feedback; if declined, continue and never ask again this session.
2. Ask the user to describe the issue in their own words; WAIT.
3. Preview "Here's what I'll send to HubSpot: [their exact words]. Should I go ahead?" and WAIT for confirmation.
4. Only call this tool once the user confirms.
</flow>

<critical_requirements>
- NEVER call without explicit user confirmation of the feedback to send.
- The feedback field MUST be the user's own words - never auto-generate or paraphrase.
- Claude/ChatGPT thumbs up/down send feedback to Anthropic/OpenAI, NOT HubSpot; only this tool sends to HubSpot.
- NEVER submit feedback about non-HubSpot tools or connectors.
</critical_requirements>

feedback.description:
User's verbatim feedback about the HubSpot connector. CRITICAL RULES:
- Use the user's EXACT words. NEVER paraphrase, summarize, or rewrite.
- If the user said it in their language, keep it in their language.
- If the user hasn't typed specific feedback yet, do NOT fill this in yourself — ask them first.
- Avoid PII — use anonymized references.

triggeringToolName.description:
Name of the HubSpot tool related to this feedback.
IMPORTANT: This tool ONLY collects feedback about HubSpot connector tools.
Do NOT submit feedback about non-HubSpot tools (e.g. Slack, Microsoft 365, Notion, iMessage, Intercom, Bash, etc.).

feedbackType.description:
Category of the feedback being submitted. Used to triage and analyze feedback trends.
- PROBLEM: Something is broken or not working as expected (errors, incorrect results, bugs).
- FEATURE_REQUEST: A request for new functionality or capability, including enhancements to existing features that would require new behavior to be built.
- GENERAL_FEEDBACK: Opinions, observations, or suggestions about an existing tool or workflow — e.g., usability impressions, praise, workflow friction, or improvement ideas that don't rise to the level of a bug report or feature request.
- OTHER: Use only when the feedback genuinely does not fit any of the above categories.

sourceInterface.description:
Where the feedback originated.
- MCP_UI: Submitted from the dedicated in-app feedback UI rendered by the MCP host (e.g. a feedback form/widget the user explicitly opened).
- NON_UI: Submitted from a regular chat conversation (no dedicated feedback UI).

openToResponse.description:
Whether the user is open to the HubSpot team responding to their feedback (e.g. to follow up once it has been acted on).
After the user has given their feedback, ask them once whether they are open to a response from the HubSpot team.
Set to true ONLY if the user explicitly says yes. If they decline, don't answer, or you didn't ask, leave it false. NEVER assume consent.

tools.name: manage_segment
tools.description:
Create, edit, convert, delete, or restore a segment, add/remove its records, or change its exclusions. Set operation.type to an operation below; segments are identified by list ID.

<mandatory_confirmation>
This tool writes to the portal. Before calling it, you MUST show the user a summary of the exact action and get explicit approval:
- CreateStaticSegmentOperation (new segment that never updates): the name, object type, and   either how many records (if any) it starts with, or its filter and each exclusion, and that   it won't update.
- CreateDynamicSegmentOperation (new self-updating segment): the name, object type, filter, and   each exclusion.
- UpdateSegmentOperation (edit in place): the segment and which of its name, description, or   filter change.
- AddMembersOperation / RemoveMembersOperation (static membership): the segment, object type,   and number of records added or removed.
- AddMembersFromSegmentOperation: the source and target segments.
- RemoveAllMembersOperation (empty it, segment kept) / DeleteSegmentOperation: the segment,   and whether it is emptied or deleted.
- RestoreSegmentOperation (undo a delete): the deleted segment and any new name.
- ConvertSegmentOperation (freeze a segment or make it active, in place; never rebuild it with   a create plus a delete): the segment and its new type.
- UpdateSegmentSuppressionOperation (exclusions): the segment and each segment, record, rule,   or email domain it starts or stops excluding.
End with an explicit approval prompt (e.g. "Proceed? [Yes / No]"). Leave confirmationStatus as UNCONFIRMED until the user approves; only after they confirm, call the tool with confirmationStatus set to CONFIRMED. Do NOT set CONFIRMED before the user approves, even if the user asks you to "just do it" or to skip confirmation. On the first confirmation in a chat you may also offer to stop asking for the rest of the session; if the user agrees, set confirmationStatus to CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION on subsequent calls.
</mandatory_confirmation>

name.description: The name for the new segment. If the user has not explicitly provided a name, ask for one before calling this tool.

objectType.description:
Mandatory field specifying the ObjectType to create the segment for.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, and other documented HubSpot objects) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` (e.g. `p885186001_fleet_vehicles`) that you MUST obtain from `discover_hubspot_schema` before searching — do not construct or guess it.
A plausible standard-looking name (e.g. `products`) may actually resolve to a different standard object OR a custom object. When you are not certain a name is a standard type, treat it as non-standard and resolve it via `discover_hubspot_schema` first, then use the exact `typeName` it returns.

memberObjectIds.description: CRM record IDs to pre-populate a hand-picked segment. Leave empty to create an empty segment; use AddMembersOperation for large batches. Leave empty when filterExpression is set: a static segment with filters takes its members from the filter, not from hand-picked IDs.

description.description: Optional short, user-friendly description of what the segment represents.

filterExpression.description:
Optional filter whose matching records fill the segment once, when it is created; it never updates after that. Set it ONLY when the user describes WHO should be in the list and wants that membership frozen. Leave it UNSET for an empty or hand-picked list, and never pass a filter crafted to match no records. When speaking to the user, call this a "static segment with filters" that won't update, and never say STATIC, DYNAMIC or "snapshot". When the user wants a list that keeps up as records change, use CreateDynamicSegmentOperation instead. Don't write exclusions into it: to keep out another segment's members, specific records, unsubscribed or non-marketing contacts, or an email domain, use the exclusion fields.

    SQL-like filter expression defining segment membership.

    Property conditions compare the object's own properties and combine with AND, OR and parentheses: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, CONTAINS_ANY (...), STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, IN (...), IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, BETWEEN x AND y. Relative dates use NOW() or TODAY() with whole-day offsets only — DAYS or WEEKS, never MONTHS/QUARTERS/YEARS (write NOW() - 90 DAYS, not NOW() - 3 MONTHS). Dates compare at day granularity, and a date property never compares = or != against a relative time (use a fixed date like '2026-08-13', or a rolling window). Example: "lifecyclestage = 'customer' AND annualrevenue > 500000". Write a value's apostrophe as two single quotes — lastname = 'O''Brien' — never with a backslash, which does not escape it.

    A != or NOT IN condition matches only records that have a value for the property; records where it is empty are left out. Include them only when the user asks, by writing (p != v OR p IS NULL) — it is stored as one condition, the segments UI's "Include records where … is empty" option, so it does not multiply like other ORs. For a property of an associated record, put that pair inside the one ASSOCIATION's braces — ASSOCIATION(...) { (p != v OR p IS NULL) } — never as two ASSOCIATIONs joined by OR. Never include them by default.

    To leave out records that match any of several combinations of conditions on two or more properties ("not any of: in Boston and a Lead; in Austin and a Customer; …"): with up to three combinations, write the negation directly, NOT ((city = 'Boston' AND lifecyclestage = 'lead') OR …); it is stored as != conditions with their usual handling of records with no value, so add nothing for those. With more, that multiplies too far to store, so it needs a helper: a segment of the records the combinations describe, excluded from the new segment. An exclusion keeps every other record, including ones with no value for those properties. Before creating anything, tell the user there are too many combinations to write as one filter, so you'll build a helper segment and exclude it, and ask whether to include records with no value for those properties (if the user already said, only confirm the helper segment). To leave them out, give the new segment p IS NOT NULL for each of those properties. A NOT over one property's values stays a single NOT IN (...).

    Keep the expression small. Before it is stored it is expanded into disjunctive normal form, so every OR multiplies: OR groups of widths w1, w2, ... produce w1 x w2 x ... branches, and every ANDed condition is copied into every branch. Branches x conditions per branch is the stored filter count, and it must stay under 250. Multiply the OR widths before writing: 8 ANDed conditions with two OR groups of 5 and 10 alternatives is 50 branches and 500 filters, already rejected. Every ASSOCIATION and NOT ASSOCIATION is copied into every branch too, and a segment holds at most 60 of those copies: one beside an OR of 30 alternatives is already 30. Several values of one property are one condition and do not multiply: p IN ('a', 'b') for exact values, p CONTAINS_ANY ('a', 'b') for substrings — never an OR of p = … or of p CONTAINS …. To fit, write those as one condition, drop redundant ANDed conditions, put ORed conditions in a helper segment referenced with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or split the audience across more than one segment; never narrow, drop or truncate the user's alternatives. A number IN (...) is stored as one filter per number, so a list of record ids (hs_object_id IN (...)) counts once per id, and inside an ASSOCIATION each id is its own association copy. A few ids fit: contacts at three given companies are ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = <id>) { hs_object_id IN (101, 202, 303) }. Only when the ids would take the segment past either limit, seed them into a hand-picked static segment of their own object type with membersToAddToStaticList and reference it with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) } for associated records.

    Property names are the object type's internal CRM property names on THIS portal — look them up via your CRM property/schema tools, never guess from display labels or other portals; a name missing from the schema fails validation. Enumeration (dropdown) values must be the internal stored value, never the display label — a wrong value is NOT rejected: the segment saves and silently matches no records, so source stored values from the property definition. There is no dotted cross-object path (company.industry = '...' is invalid); conditions on a related record go inside ASSOCIATION(...) braces.

    Engagement conditions (opened, clicked, visited, submitted, last engaged) often have two valid encodings: a filter form below, or an analytics property on the object itself (recency dates, counts). When no matching filter form or event exists — or the request spans ANY asset rather than a specific one — search the object's real properties for an equivalent before reporting the condition unsupported (the look-it-up rule still applies).

    Sourcing ids — users do not know these ids; look them up, never invent one (a guessed id creates a segment that silently filters on the wrong thing): list ids from searchSegments; association type ids, event type ids, event property names, form guids, workflow ids, import ids and email triples from searchFilterInputs (kind ASSOCIATION, EVENT, EVENT_PROPERTY, FORM, WORKFLOW, IMPORT or EMAIL), whose results include ready-to-use filter fragments.

anyOf.description:
Edit an existing segment's name, description, or filter in place. This is a partial update: only
 the fields provided change; omitted fields keep their current values. It does NOT change
 membership directly (use AddMembersOperation / RemoveMembersOperation) and does NOT convert a
 hand-picked static list into a filter-driven one.

listId.description: The ID of the STATIC segment to remove every member from. This empties the segment's membership; it does not delete the segment, which remains and becomes empty (use DeleteSegmentOperation to remove the segment itself). Emptying runs as a background bulk operation, so the segment clears shortly rather than instantly. DYNAMIC (filter-driven) segments are rejected: their membership is computed from their filter and cannot be emptied manually — change the filter via UpdateSegmentOperation instead.

The ID of the segment to permanently delete. This removes the segment itself (not just its members); to empty a static segment while keeping it, use RemoveAllMembersOperation instead. Works for STATIC and DYNAMIC segments. Deleting a segment does not delete the CRM records in it. This is destructive, so confirm the exact segment with the user first; a deleted segment can be brought back with RestoreSegmentOperation. A segment that another segment's filter or exclusions still use can't be deleted until that use is removed: the other segment's filter can be changed with UpdateSegmentOperation and its exclusions with UpdateSegmentSuppressionOperation, after asking the user.

The list ID of the deleted segment to restore, from a DeleteSegmentOperation earlier in the conversation or a querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery with deleted=true. It comes back with its filters and settings under the same list ID; a DYNAMIC segment then recalculates its members, and a STATIC segment's members return in the background.

newName.description: A new name to restore the segment under. Omit it to keep the original name; set it only after a restore was refused because another segment now has that name, to the name the user chose.

anyOf.description:
Restore a deleted segment. This brings back the same segment under its original list ID, so it is
 the way to undo a DeleteSegmentOperation: recreating the segment makes a new list with a new ID,
 and anything that used the old one stays pointed at the deleted segment.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment whose exclusions to edit. Must be a DYNAMIC segment or a STATIC segment built from a filter; a hand-picked STATIC segment has no base audience to exclude from.

addExcludedSegmentIds.description: List IDs of segments to START excluding the members of. Added to any segments already excluded (this never clears existing exclusions); find these IDs with querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery. Excluding a segment holds its members out of this one at the top level, distinct from a not-in-list filter condition.

removeExcludedSegmentIds.description: List IDs of segments to STOP excluding. Their members rejoin the segment where they match its filter, so the audience grows. An ID that is not currently excluded is ignored.

addExcludedRecordIds.description: Record IDs to START excluding, of the segment's own object type (e.g. contact IDs for a contact segment). Each is kept out of the segment even if it matches the filter, without changing the record or the filter; this is how to take specific records off a DYNAMIC segment. Added to any records already excluded. At most 200 per call.

removeExcludedRecordIds.description: Record IDs to STOP excluding. They rejoin the segment if they match its filter; an ID that is not currently excluded is ignored. At most 200 per call.

excludeUnsubscribers.description: Set true to exclude contacts who have unsubscribed from all email, false to stop excluding them, or omit to keep the current setting. Contact segments only.

excludeNonMarketingContacts.description: Set true to exclude non-marketing contacts, false to stop excluding them, or omit to keep the current setting. Contact segments only.

addExcludedEmailDomains.description: Email domains to START excluding, e.g. "example.com". Added to any domains already excluded. Contact segments only.

removeExcludedEmailDomains.description: Email domains to STOP excluding. Removed from those currently excluded.

anyOf.description:
Edit an existing segment's exclusion (suppression) settings by an add/remove delta: segments
 whose members to hold out, individual records to hold out, and, for contact segments, the
 unsubscriber, non-marketing-contact, and email-domain exclusion rules. Only what is named
 changes; every other exclusion carries forward. It does not change the segment's filter or any
 record.

listId.description: The list ID of the STATIC segment to add the members to. The user needs edit access to it. A DYNAMIC segment is refused, since its members come from its filter; the refusal lists what to offer the user instead.

sourceListId.description: The list ID of the segment whose current members to copy, found with querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery. It may be DYNAMIC or STATIC, but must hold the same object type as the segment they are added to. Use this, not GetSegmentMembersQuery plus AddMembersOperation, to put one segment's members into another. To keep a segment's members OUT, exclude it with UpdateSegmentSuppressionOperation instead; to keep up with the source as it changes, filter on its membership instead.

copyEveryMember.description: Set true only when the user confirmed copying a large segment after membersCopy.status came back NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, or had already said to copy all of them however many there are. A plain request to add a segment's members is not that, so leave it false: the tool then copies nothing and asks for confirmation first when the segment is large.

anyOf.description:
Copy every current member of one segment into a STATIC segment, without listing their record IDs.
 A one-time copy: records that join the source later are not added.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment to convert, found with querySegments SearchSegmentsQuery. It keeps this list ID, its name, filters and exclusions, so the emails, workflows and other segments that use it stay connected. That is why this, never a create operation followed by DeleteSegmentOperation, is how to freeze a segment or make one active: a rebuilt segment gets a new list ID, and nothing that used the old one is reconnected.

convertTo.description: The type to convert the segment to. STATIC freezes a DYNAMIC segment with the members it has now: it stops updating, and records can then be added or removed by hand. Do it when the user asks ("stop it updating", "make it static", "lock in who's in it now"). DYNAMIC makes a STATIC segment built from filters update automatically again ("make it active", "keep it up to date"); its members are then recalculated from its filters. A hand-picked STATIC segment has no filters, so it can't become DYNAMIC; the refusal says what to offer instead.

confirmedMembersChange.description: Set true only when converting to DYNAMIC and the user confirmed, after conversion.status came back NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, that the segment's members will be recalculated from its filters, so records added or removed by hand don't stay that way. Leave it false otherwise: a conversion to DYNAMIC then changes nothing and asks for that confirmation first.

anyOf.description:
Convert an existing segment between DYNAMIC (active) and STATIC in place. It keeps its list ID, so
 whatever uses it stays connected, which a new segment built to replace it would not.

operation.description: The segment operation to perform. Set type to CreateStaticSegmentOperation, CreateDynamicSegmentOperation, UpdateSegmentOperation, AddMembersOperation, or RemoveMembersOperation.

confirmationStatus.description: User confirmation for this write. Defaults to UNCONFIRMED; the write is rejected unless set to CONFIRMED (or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION) after the user approves.

tools.name: manage_landing_page
tools.description: Create, edit, style, publish, clone, and inspect HubSpot landing pages. One action per call. Reads: MODULES, MODULE_TYPES, MODULE_DEF, MODULE_STYLES, MODULE_GUIDE, REVISIONS, TEMPLATES, FORMS, BRAND_KIT, LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES. Writes: CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_MODULE, UPDATE_MODULE, SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, INSERT, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE, SET_METADATA, PUBLISH, CLONE, CLONE_VARIANTS, RESTORE_REVISION. Read before write: MODULES before any edit; MODULE_TYPES before INSERT; MODULE_DEF before unfamiliar fields; MODULE_STYLES before SET_MODULE_STYLES. Writes mutate one shared draft — never concurrently. CREATE_MODULE authors a reusable custom module TYPE (not on any page — check LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES first, then INSERT the returned modulePath). BATCH IS THE DEFAULT for compound edits: group SET_MODULE_FIELDS/STYLES/SECTION_STYLES/METADATA/REMOVE/MOVE into one action=BATCH call (operationsJson, sequential server-side, returns batchResults). Max 10 operations; at most one REMOVE/REMOVE_SECTION/MOVE per batch. NOT batchable (always separate): INSERT/CREATE_*/UPDATE_*/CLONE/PUBLISH/RESTORE_REVISION. If BATCH returns "not currently supported", fall back to sequential calls. CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE requires explicit user confirmation IN CHAT — choosing a template is NOT confirmation. Confirm before PUBLISH/RESTORE_REVISION/UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. Never renders a card — after your LAST edit or PUBLISH, call the render tool. Examples: action=MODULES contentId=123 -> modulesJson. action=CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE pageName="Spring Promo" templatePath="..." -> {status,contentId,editorUrl}. action=SET_MODULE_FIELDS contentId=456 moduleId="hero_1" fieldOverridesJson={headline:"Hi"} -> verifiedFieldsJson. action=SET_SECTION_STYLES contentId=456 moduleId="hero_1" stylesJson={backgroundColor:{r:255,g:238,b:0,a:1}} -> verifiedStylesJson. Scopes: reads need landingpages-read or -write; writes need landingpages-write; PUBLISH also needs landingpages-publish.

action.description: Action to perform. One per call. READ actions (no side effects): "MODULES": list every module on the page draft. Each entry includes the module's field values, its layout position (sectionId, rowIndex, parentCellName when it lives inside a nested column, and cellWidth/cellX on the 12-column grid), and ownership flags (overrideable, globalOwned, globalPartialPath, themePartialOwned). Positions are populated even on a freshly created template page, before any edit. Capture a module's position here BEFORE you REMOVE or MOVE it so you can restore or reposition it precisely. Check ownership before REMOVE/MOVE: true global partials (header/footer) and global widgets are refused, but modules inside theme dnd_partial sections are removable and movable. "MODULE_TYPES": list available module types for this page's theme (call before INSERT). "MODULE_DEF": full field schema for a module type (requires modulePath). The response also includes the curated guide in moduleGuide when one exists, so a separate MODULE_GUIDE call is usually unnecessary. "MODULE_STYLES": read the layout styles (padding, margin, background, visibility) for a module (requires moduleId). "MODULE_GUIDE": (rarely needed — MODULE_DEF already returns the same guide inline) curated markdown for the modulePath covering required fields, common traps, and a minimal INSERT body. Errors if no guide exists; check MODULE_TYPES.hasGuide first. "REVISIONS": list recent page revisions for undo. "TEMPLATES": list landing page templates available in the portal (contentId not required). "FORMS": list forms available in the portal for embedding on THIS LANDING PAGE via the @hubspot/form module (contentId not required). This is the landing-page tool's own forms lookup and it is complete: an empty list means the portal has no forms. Never call manage_website_page (or a CRM tool) for form data while working on a landing page. Returns guid, name, portalId, formType, isPublished, createdAt, updatedAt. "BRAND_KIT": fetch the portal's primary brand kit (colors, fonts, logos) for THIS LANDING PAGE — complete on its own, and never to be re-fetched via manage_website_page — when brand-consistent content would help — e.g. picking a CTA color, a hero font, or a logo to drop into a header (contentId not required). "LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES": list the custom module types already in this portal's Design Manager, most recently updated first (contentId not required). Call this BEFORE CREATE_MODULE to check whether a suitable module already exists — reusing one is cheaper than creating a duplicate, and its modulePath goes straight into INSERT. Returns customModules (modulePath plus a compact field schema). Optional: limit (default 20, max 50). WRITE actions (mutate the same shared draft — issue them ONE AT A TIME, never in parallel): "CLONE": duplicate an existing page (requires contentId of the source page; optional pageName, slug and businessUnitId for the clone). Returns a new contentId. "CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE": create the page from a template (requires pageName and templatePath; optional slug and businessUnitId). MUST be preceded by a proposal card (call render_landing_page_ui directly with a "propose" target — there is no separate write step to propose) and an explicit user confirmation IN CHAT — never the first step of creating a page, and choosing a template is NOT confirmation. Returns contentId. "SET_MODULE_FIELDS": set field values on one module (requires contentId, moduleId, fieldOverridesJson). Each top-level field you send REPLACES its stored value in full — objects and lists are NOT deep-merged, so to change one part of a field send its whole current value from action=MODULES (see fieldOverridesJson). "SET_MODULE_STYLES": set layout styles (padding, margin, background, visibility) on one module (requires contentId, moduleId, stylesJson). Merge semantics — only supplied fields are updated. Call action=MODULE_STYLES first to see current values. "SET_SECTION_STYLES": set the background, padding, margin, or full-width of the ENTIRE SECTION band a module sits in (requires contentId, moduleId, stylesJson; moduleId is any module inside the band, used as an anchor). This is the correct way to do "make this section's background <color>" — do NOT inject CSS via SET_METADATA headHtml for section backgrounds. Merge semantics. Page-scoped bands — including theme dnd_partial sections — CAN be styled; only true global sections (header/footer/global widgets) are refused. "INSERT": add a new module (requires contentId, modulePath; then EITHER anchorModuleId+anchorPosition for anchor-based placement, OR sectionId+rowStart+columnStart+columnsSpanned for grid-coord placement; optional fieldOverridesJson). "REMOVE": delete one module (requires contentId, moduleId). If it was the last module in its section band, the now-empty band — background and padding included — is collapsed too, so no empty "Drop modules here" ghost band is left behind. "REMOVE_SECTION": delete the ENTIRE section band a module sits in — the whole top-level row, every module in it, AND the band's own background/padding styles (requires contentId, moduleId; moduleId is any module inside the target band, used as an anchor). Page-scoped sections — including theme dnd_partial sections like a logo bar — CAN be removed; only true global sections are refused. "MOVE": reposition module into its own new row (requires contentId, moduleId; then EITHER anchorModuleId+anchorPosition for anchor-based placement, OR sectionId+rowStart for grid placement). For MOVE, anchorPosition supports the new-row directions BEFORE / AFTER / START_OF_SECTION / END_OF_SECTION; in-row and stacked directions (IN_ROW_*, STACK_*) are INSERT-only — to place a module in-row or stacked, REMOVE it and INSERT with that anchorPosition. "SET_METADATA": update page metadata — pageName, htmlTitle, slug, metaDescription, featuredImageUrl, language, headHtml, noIndex, targetAccount (requires contentId; all metadata fields optional). "PUBLISH": publish draft (requires contentId; confirm with the user first). To publish several pages in one call, pass contentIds (up to 10) instead of contentId; each page succeeds or fails on its own and pageResults reports each. "CLONE_VARIANTS": create up to 10 personalized copies of one source page in ONE call (requires contentId of the source and variants). Each variant is cloned, its module fields are patched, and its metadata is set, all server-side. Use it instead of CLONE + BATCH per page whenever you are making several variants of the same page: module IDs on a clone are the same as on the source, so read MODULES on the source once. Returns pageResults, one per variant. "RESTORE_REVISION": roll back to revision (requires contentId, revisionId; confirm first). "CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE": create a fully custom landing page from HubL source you write. Use when no existing template fits the user's design — you author the complete HTML/HubL and pass it as hublSource. Requires slug and hublSource. Returns templatePath (always .html). No module editing is needed — the HubL IS the final design. hublSource must be under 1.5 MB. "UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE": replace the ENTIRE HubL source of a page previously created with CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. Requires templatePath (from the create response) and hublSource; pass templateId too when you have it — it resolves the template even after a publish moves it. The change is LIVE the moment the call succeeds: every page built on the template, a published one included, renders the new source at once. There is no draft stage and no publish step, and the previous source cannot be read back. Confirm with the user first, and say when a published page will change. Use it only to change a design whose source you wrote earlier in this conversation. In a fresh session you do not have the current source, so author the changed design with CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE and CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE as a new page; replace an existing template only when the user explicitly asks to overwrite its design wholesale and confirms. Same hublSource size limit as CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. "CREATE_MODULE": author a NEW custom module TYPE in Design Manager — a reusable module the theme does not have yet (requires moduleName, moduleHtml, moduleFieldsJson; contentId not required). Returns modulePath. This creates the TYPE only and puts nothing on any page: pass modulePath verbatim to action=INSERT to place an instance. Reach for it only when no built-in or existing custom module fits (check MODULE_TYPES and LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES first). Not tied to a page, so several CREATE_MODULE calls CAN run in parallel. "UPDATE_MODULE": replace the HubL and/or field schema of a module type previously created with CREATE_MODULE (requires modulePath from the create response, plus moduleHtml and/or moduleFieldsJson). moduleFieldsJson REPLACES the whole schema rather than patching it. Every page using the module re-renders with the new source immediately. Only module types created through CREATE_MODULE can be updated. "BATCH": run several operations in ONE call, executed sequentially server-side, stopping at the first failure (requires operationsJson). Batchable sub-actions: all READ actions, plus the write actions SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, SET_METADATA, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE — i.e. edits on modules/sections you ALREADY have IDs for. NOT batchable (their output feeds later work, or they change whole-page lifecycle): INSERT, CLONE, CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, CREATE_MODULE, UPDATE_MODULE, PUBLISH, RESTORE_REVISION, BATCH. Returns batchResults with a per-operation outcome; committed operations are NOT rolled back when a later operation fails. Read MODULES first to capture the IDs each operation needs.

contentId.description: Content ID of the landing page. Required for most actions. NOT required for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE (creates a new page), TEMPLATES, FORMS, BRAND_KIT, MODULE_DEF, and MODULE_GUIDE.

moduleId.description: Module ID to operate on. Required for SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE, and MODULE_STYLES. For REMOVE_SECTION and SET_SECTION_STYLES it is any module inside the target section band (an anchor). Find IDs via action=MODULES.

modulePath.description: Module type path (e.g. "@hubspot/rich_text"). Required for INSERT, MODULE_DEF, MODULE_GUIDE, and UPDATE_MODULE. Use paths exactly as returned by action=MODULE_TYPES, LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES, or CREATE_MODULE (a custom module's stored path can differ from the moduleName you sent, so never reconstruct it).

query.description: Substring filter. When action=MODULE_TYPES: filters by module type name. When action=TEMPLATES: filters by template name.

availableForNewContent.description: When action=TEMPLATES: filter to templates available for new page creation. Omit to return all templates.

folderName.description: When action=TEMPLATES: filter by folder name (e.g. "my-theme/templates").

themePath.description: When action=TEMPLATES: filter templates by theme path. Use for HubSpot themes ("@hubspot/elevate", "@hubspot/growth"), marketplace themes ("@marketplace/vendor/theme-name"), or custom themes ("my-custom-theme"). Omit to return templates across all themes.

responseFormat.description: Verbosity of the response. "DETAILED" returns all fields and is the default when omitted. "SUMMARY" trims verbose fields to save tokens on large pages: when action=MODULES, drops module field values and returns only module IDs, modulePaths, and section info. For MODULE_TYPES, MODULE_DEF, and REVISIONS, SUMMARY currently returns the same payload as DETAILED.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return for paginated read actions (MODULES, MODULE_TYPES, REVISIONS). Defaults to 50. Ignored for MODULE_DEF. For LIST_CUSTOM_MODULES it defaults to 20 and is capped at 50.

offset.description: Zero-based starting index for paginated read actions (MODULES, MODULE_TYPES, REVISIONS). Defaults to 0. Use the response's nextOffset to fetch the next page when hasMore is true. Ignored for MODULE_DEF.

pageName.description: Name for the landing page. Required for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE. Optional for CLONE (defaults to a copy of the source page name). Also used by SET_METADATA to update the internal listing name shown in the HubSpot content listing UI (not the HTML title).

templatePath.description: Template path to build the page on. Required for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE. Use action=TEMPLATES to discover available templates, then pass the templatePath exactly as returned.

templateId.description: Numeric template id, as returned by action=TEMPLATES ("id") and by CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE / UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE ("templateId"). Optional for UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE, where it is preferred over templatePath: publishing can move a custom template to a different path, and the id keeps working when it does. Ignored by every other action.

fieldOverridesJson.description: JSON object of field values keyed by top-level field name (e.g. {"heading":"Close deals faster"}). Required for SET_MODULE_FIELDS. Optional for INSERT (sets initial field values on the new module). On SET_MODULE_FIELDS each key REPLACES that field's whole stored value; fields you omit are unchanged. Objects and lists are NOT deep-merged: a sub-field left out of a sent object or list item reverts to the module default (or is cleared), and list items left out are deleted. To change one sub-field or one list item (e.g. one card's text), copy the field's current value from action=MODULES, change only that part, and send the whole value. Dotted or indexed keys like "groupStyle.headingStyleVariant" or "cards[0].title" are not field names and are rejected.

stylesJson.description: JSON object of structured layout styles to merge. Required for SET_MODULE_STYLES (onto a module) and SET_SECTION_STYLES (onto a section band). Uses merge semantics: only supplied fields are updated, existing styles are preserved. Shape: {"breakpoint_styles":{"default":{"padding":{"top":{"value":20,"units":"px"}},"margin":{"top":{"value":10,"units":"px"}}}}}. Supported breakpoints: "default" (desktop), "mobile". Supported spacing sides — padding: top, right, bottom, left; margin: top, bottom. Each side is a Size: {"value":<number>,"units":"px"|"em"|"rem"|..."}. Background color (mainly for SET_SECTION_STYLES) goes in the top-level backgroundColor field as r/g/b/a: {"backgroundColor":{"r":255,"g":238,"b":0,"a":1}} (r/g/b 0–255, a 0–1). Section-only fields (SET_SECTION_STYLES): "forceFullWidthSection":true OR "maxWidthSectionCentering":<px> (mutually exclusive). Use camelCase keys (e.g. backgroundColor, breakpointStyles, forceFullWidthSection) — they mirror what action=MODULE_STYLES returns. Also supports per-breakpoint "hidden":true/false to toggle visibility. Layout only — for TEXT color use the separate textColor field, not this.

textColor.description: For action=SET_MODULE_STYLES: set the text color of ALL text in a module (headings, paragraphs, list items) to this CSS color, e.g. "#cc0000", "red", or "rgb(204,0,0)". This is the reliable way to recolor module text — it writes a scoped, !important rule the renderer applies to the module's own elements, overriding the theme. Do NOT hand-roll headHtml CSS for text color, and do NOT use it to recolor a whole section (use the section's sectionStyleVariant for that). Supply with moduleId; may be combined with stylesJson.

sectionId.description: Layout section ID to place the module in. Required for INSERT (grid-coord placement). Optional for MOVE (omit to keep current section). Find section IDs via action=MODULES.

rowStart.description: 1-based row position within the section. Required for INSERT (grid-coord placement). Optional for MOVE. Modules with the same rowStart and sectionId are placed side-by-side.

columnStart.description: 1-based column position on a 12-column grid. Required for INSERT (grid-coord placement). Optional for MOVE. columnStart=1 is leftmost.

columnsSpanned.description: Width in columns on the 12-column grid. Required for INSERT when using legacy grid-coord placement. Full width=12, two halves=6 each, three thirds=4 each. Omit when using anchor-based placement (anchorModuleId + anchorPosition) — width is computed automatically by stealing from siblings.

anchorModuleId.description: Anchor-based placement: moduleId of an existing module that an INSERT (or a moved module on MOVE) should land relative to. When provided, omit rowStart / columnStart / columnsSpanned — the backend resolves the target row from the anchor and (for INSERT) auto-redistributes column widths across siblings. Pair with anchorPosition.

anchorPosition.description: Anchor placement direction. Used with anchorModuleId on INSERT. Values: "BEFORE" (new module on a new row immediately above the anchor's row), "AFTER" (new row immediately below), "IN_ROW_WITH" (sibling cell appended to the right of all existing cells in the anchor's row — siblings give up width), "IN_ROW_BEFORE" (sibling cell positioned to the LEFT of the anchor within the same row), "IN_ROW_AFTER" (sibling cell positioned to the RIGHT of the anchor within the same row, regardless of any cells beyond the anchor), "START_OF_SECTION" (first row of anchor's section), "END_OF_SECTION" (last row of anchor's section), "STACK_ABOVE" (wrap the anchor in a column and place the new module ABOVE it as a stacked row), "STACK_BELOW" (same, stacked BELOW). STACK_* builds a "unified section" — both modules share ONE wrapper cell as separate rows (the shape the editor's drag-to-stack creates); use it instead of BEFORE/AFTER when the two modules should read as one visual group rather than independent section rows. STACK requires a module anchor inside a section (not a top-level section id).

htmlTitle.description: HTML <title> tag for the page (~50–60 chars). Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

slug.description: URL slug (lowercase, hyphenated, no leading slash). Used for SET_METADATA (omit to leave unchanged), CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE (omit to derive from pageName), CLONE (omit to auto-generate), or CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE (required — used as the template name).

metaDescription.description: Meta description for search snippets (~140–160 chars). Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

featuredImageUrl.description: Featured image URL for social sharing. Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

language.description: ISO-639-1 language code (e.g. "en", "de"). Used for SET_METADATA (omit to leave unchanged).

headHtml.description: Raw HTML injected into <head> (e.g. "<style>body{background:#2563eb}</style>"). Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

noIndex.description: true keeps the page out of search engines by adding <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> to its head HTML (replacing any other robots tag); false removes a noindex robots tag. Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged. Use it for pages meant to be reached only from a link, such as a page personalized for one account's ads or outreach.

targetAccount.description: CRM record ID of the company (object type 0-2) the page is personalized for. Stored on the page itself, where it shows as the page record's Target Account, so it survives later edits and publishes. Only used for SET_METADATA. Omit to leave unchanged.

revisionId.description: Revision ID to restore. Required for RESTORE_REVISION. Find IDs via action=REVISIONS.

hublSource.description: Complete HubL template source. Required for CREATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE and UPDATE_CUSTOM_TEMPLATE. Must be a valid HubL document — real HubL expressions, not escaped HTML. {{ standard_header_includes }} and {{ standard_footer_includes }} are injected automatically before </head> and before </body> if absent. Accepted size: up to 1,500,000 bytes of UTF-8 (1.5 MB).

operationsJson.description: Required for action=BATCH. JSON array of operations to run sequentially, in order. Each element is an object shaped like a single manage_landing_page request: {"action":"...", ...the fields that action needs}. Example: [{"action":"SET_MODULE_FIELDS","contentId":123,"moduleId":"m1","fieldOverridesJson":"{\"heading\":\"Hi\"}"},{"action":"REMOVE","contentId":123,"moduleId":"m2"}]. Only batchable sub-actions are allowed (all READ actions, plus SET_MODULE_FIELDS, SET_MODULE_STYLES, SET_SECTION_STYLES, SET_METADATA, REMOVE, REMOVE_SECTION, MOVE); INSERT, the CREATE/CLONE/UPDATE lifecycle actions, PUBLISH, RESTORE_REVISION, and nested BATCH are rejected before anything runs. The batch STOPS at the first failing operation: operations before it stay committed (there is no rollback), and operations after it are reported as "skipped". The array size must not exceed the server's configured maximum. Each operation's own required fields (contentId, moduleId, etc.) must be present on that element.

businessUnitId.description: ID of the business unit (brand) to put the page in. Used for CREATE_FROM_TEMPLATE and CLONE. Omit or pass 0 for the account's default business unit (CLONE then keeps the source page's business unit).

moduleName.description: Display name for a custom module type, as it appears in the editor's module list (e.g. "Pricing Card"). Required for CREATE_MODULE, optional for UPDATE_MODULE. Also seeds the module's Design Manager path, so keep it short and specific.

moduleHtml.description: HubL template source for a custom module — the markup one instance of it renders (e.g. "<section>{{ module.heading }}</section>"). Reference each field from moduleFieldsJson as {{ module.<fieldName> }}. Required for CREATE_MODULE; on UPDATE_MODULE supply it only to replace the source. Pass real HubL, not escaped HTML.

moduleFieldsJson.description: Field schema for a custom module: a JSON ARRAY of field definitions, each with name, type, label and default — e.g. [{"name":"heading","type":"text","label":"Heading","default":"Hello"}]. This is the module's SCHEMA (what an editor can fill in), not content values. Required for CREATE_MODULE. On UPDATE_MODULE it REPLACES the entire schema — send every field you want to keep.

label.description: Who this copy is for, such as the account or segment name. Echoed back in pageResults.

pageName.description: Internal name of the new page.

slug.description: URL slug of the new page (lowercase, hyphenated, no leading slash). Each copy needs its own. Omit to auto-generate.

htmlTitle.description: HTML <title> of the new page. Omit to keep the source page's.

metaDescription.description: Meta description of the new page. Omit to keep the source page's.

headHtml.description: Raw HTML for the new page's <head>, as for SET_METADATA. Omit to keep the source page's.

noIndex.description: true keeps the new page out of search engines; false removes a noindex robots tag it inherited. Omit to keep the source page's setting.

targetAccount.description: CRM record ID of the company (object type 0-2) this copy is personalized for.

moduleId.description: Module ID from the SOURCE page's MODULES read. A copy keeps every module ID of its source.

fieldOverridesJson.description: JSON object of verbatim field values for this module, exactly as for SET_MODULE_FIELDS fieldOverridesJson (e.g. {"heading":"Close deals faster"}).

moduleFields.description: Field values to change on this copy, one entry per module. Modules you leave out keep the source page's content.

variants.description: For action=CLONE_VARIANTS only: the copies of the source page (contentId) to create, up to 10 per call. Every moduleId is checked against the source before anything is cloned. Copies are processed independently: one failing does not stop the others.

contentIds.description: For action=PUBLISH only: content IDs of up to 10 pages to publish in one call, instead of contentId. Each page is published independently and reported in pageResults. Every other action takes contentId.

tools.name: get_aeo_metrics
tools.description:
Portal-level AEO analytics: brand visibility, mentions, citations, competitor
share-of-voice, and per-assistant breakdowns for a date window. Select the
sections you need with `include`, a JSON array of section names, e.g.
["SUMMARY", "PROMPTS"] (SUMMARY, PROMPTS, CITATIONS, CITATION_ANALYSIS,
COMPETITORS, ASSISTANT_BREAKDOWN, RUN_STATUS, ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS, BUSINESS_UNITS,
LIMITS); defaults to {SUMMARY, RUN_STATUS}. businessUnitId is optional: omit it to use
the portal's business unit automatically, or call once with
include=["BUSINESS_UNITS"] first to choose one when the portal has several.
CITATION_ANALYSIS additionally requires a citationUrl.
Dates are ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD); default to the last 30 days. Call
tool_guidance (mcpToolInstructions) for the full section catalog, setup-status
semantics, and field-level details.

businessUnitId.description: Business unit ID (optional). Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["BUSINESS_UNITS"] first to discover all available business unit IDs for this portal — data is keyed by the IDs returned there.

startDate.description: ISO-8601 start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to 30 days ago. Only set when the user asks for a different window.

endDate.description: ISO-8601 end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to today. Must be on or after startDate.

include.description: Which sections to populate, as a JSON array of section names — always an array, even for a single section (e.g. ["SUMMARY", "PROMPTS"]), never a bare string. SUMMARY = portal aggregates. PROMPTS = per-prompt metrics list. CITATIONS = citation counts + top domains with ownership flags. COMPETITORS = per-brand mention counts and share-of-voice. ASSISTANT_BREAKDOWN = metrics split by AI assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.). RUN_STATUS = run freshness. ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS = the business unit's ICPs and products (ids + names/descriptions) for use as icpIds / productIds when creating prompts. BUSINESS_UNITS = available business unit IDs and names, plus the resolved BU used for this request. LIMITS = prompt usage vs capacity (promptsUsed, promptsCapacity, onCredits, managePromptsUrl). CITATION_ANALYSIS = single-URL deep dive for citationUrl (required): per-assistant citation counts, brand mentions with relationship type, content type, and citing prompts. Defaults to {SUMMARY, RUN_STATUS}.

filters.description: Optional filters for the SUMMARY and PROMPTS sections: buying-journey phase, tracking status, visibility-score range, product / ICP / topic / language. Topic/group filters match ANY selected group by default; set groupFilterMode to ALL to require every selected group. Does not affect CITATIONS, COMPETITORS, or ASSISTANT_BREAKDOWN, which are always portal-wide.

models.description: AI models to include when PROMPTS is requested. Empty = all models. Valid values from the AEO config tool.

assistants.description: AI assistant families to include when PROMPTS is requested. Empty = all assistants. Valid values from the AEO config tool.

maxPrompts.description: Maximum number of prompts to return per page when PROMPTS is requested. Defaults to 100 and is capped at 250 to keep responses within the MCP response budget. When more prompts match than fit in one page, the PROMPTS section returns hasMore=true and a nextCursor to pass back as promptsCursor.

promptsCursor.description: Pagination cursor for the PROMPTS section. Omit (or pass 0) to start at the first page; to page through all prompts, pass the nextCursor value returned in the PROMPTS section of the previous response. Only affects the PROMPTS section.

compareToPreviousPeriod.description: Set to true to also return how the SUMMARY metrics changed versus the immediately preceding period of equal length — answering "is my AI-search visibility going up or down?". Populates summary.comparison with the prior period's values and the deltas. Adds one extra aggregation, so only set it when the user asks about a trend, change, or improvement. Only affects SUMMARY.

promptSortBy.description: Field the PROMPTS section is sorted by. CREATED_AT (default) = prompt creation time. VISIBILITY_SCORE = visibility score. CITATION_COUNT = number of citations. The URL is normalized (tracking query params stripped, trailing slash / www removed, host lowercased) before matching, so pass it exactly as it appears in that citationUrls list.

tools.name: discover_hubspot_schema
tools.description:
Discovers HubSpot data types, pipelines, and stages, and the current user's read/write access to each type. Returned type names are the values other tools accept as object types.

<usage_guidance>
- Use this tool FIRST to identify which data types exist before querying data
- Use SEARCH_OBJECT_TYPES when you don't know the exact type name. For an ambiguous term (e.g. "products": standard Products or a custom object), review all candidates, not just the top hit, and ask the user if more than one fits
- Use GET_OBJECT_TYPES when you know the type names (e.g. CONTACT, DEAL), or with an empty typeNameFilter to list all types. Also use it to check what the user can view or edit (writeAccess before any create or update)
- Use GET_PIPELINES to list a type's pipelines and stages. Stage `probability` (DEAL) is the 0-1 chance of closing won; `state` (other types) is OPEN or CLOSED, except LEAD: NEW/IN_PROGRESS are open, QUALIFIED/UNQUALIFIED are closed
- Mention a non-AVAILABLE status only if the task needs that type
</usage_guidance>

Non-AVAILABLE access statuses (readAccess/writeAccess):
- REQUIRES_REAUTHORIZATION: disconnect and reconnect the connector
- REQUIRES_PERMISSION_MODIFICATION: user lacks a HubSpot permission
- REQUIRES_ACCOUNT_MODIFICATION: account needs an upgrade
- BLOCKED_FOR_PORTALS_WITH_SENSITIVE_DATA: sensitive data, unresolvable
- NOT_AVAILABLE: unfixable, except activating a DEACTIVATED/UNKNOWN type

<examples>
  <example>
    <user_input>How many support requests did we get last month?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "SEARCH_OBJECT_TYPES", "searchTerms": "support requests tickets"}}</tool_call>
  </example>

  <example>
    <user_input>Which CRM objects can I edit?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "GET_OBJECT_TYPES"}}</tool_call>
  </example>

  <example>
    <user_input>What are the deal pipeline stages?</user_input>
    <tool_call>{"query": {"_queryType": "GET_PIPELINES", "objectType": "DEAL"}}</tool_call>
  </example>
</examples>

fetchOptions.description: Optional extra data to include in each result. Use DESCRIPTION to include type descriptions. Use READ_GUIDANCE for reading/querying tips. Use WRITE_GUIDANCE for creation/update tips. Use DEFAULT_PROPERTIES to include the default set of property names fetched for this type. If omitted, only the type name, category, and access information is returned.

tools.name: get_content_analytics_report
tools.description: Run a content analytics report across landing pages, website pages, and blog posts in the portal. Returns: TOTALS: ranked rows of contentId, contentTitle, and the requested metric value. TIME_SERIES: per-contentId series of {timestamp, value} points for the requested metric and period. SUMMARY: aggregated per-period points (one value per bucket) for the requested metric. PEOPLE: list of contacts/visitors (contactId or session identifier, plus available identity fields) who viewed the specified contentIds. Pick mode by intent: TOTALS to rank, TIME_SERIES to chart trends per page, SUMMARY for a single aggregated trend, PEOPLE for who-viewed lookups. TIME_SERIES/PEOPLE require contentIds. Examples: mode=TOTALS metric=VIEWS limit=10 -> top 10 pages by views. mode=TIME_SERIES contentIds=[123] metric=SUBMISSIONS period=LAST_30_DAYS -> daily submissions for page 123. exactly one `operation`, a JSON object (not a string) with an `_operationType`
field set to LIST (recommendations for a business unit, filterable by
status/prompt and paginated via cursor/hasMore/nextCursor; omits justification and
citations), DETAIL (one recommendation with its justification, full citation list,
and action-status fields), or
