tools.name: search_conversations
tools.description:
Search and read conversation threads and ticket or support-case messages from HubSpot inboxes. For the messages of a CONTACT, TICKET, DEAL, or COMPANY, including when summarizing a ticket, use this tool: search_crm_objects and get_crm_objects return record properties, not the thread. Resolve the record ID with search_crm_objects if needed, then pass objectType + objectId. NOTE, EMAIL, and CALL engagements don't hold inbox transcripts. Internal notes live in the thread: set includeAllDialogue=true with includeMessages=true.

Pick one mode per call: CRM object (objectType + objectId), time range (startTime/endTime), text search (query and searchMethod, optionally with a time range), or aggregation (aggregationDimensions). With no mode, it returns the most recent conversations. Time-range mode matches conversations active in the window (hs_lastmodifieddate); aggregation counts those started in it (hs_started_at).

<usage_guidance>
- For "my conversations", filter with assignedAgentId
- Name agents from assignedAgentName, or senderName with messageDetail=FULL, never from message text or signatures
- If a name matches several CRM object types, search each
- Use KEYWORD when distinctive terms (product names, error codes, jargon) would appear verbatim, even in a loosely phrased question; SEMANTIC for a described situation, a paraphrase, or another language
- One focused search is almost always enough: summarize relevant results instead of re-running reworded queries or firing parallel variations. If nothing relevant comes back, say so; an empty search is already retried with the other method
- Paginate only with the nextPageAfter a response returns, passed back verbatim as after; never build, increment, or guess a cursor. A response without nextPageAfter is the last page, so stop
- For support themes, read a small time-range sample and say it is a sample; aggregation gives volume, not topics
- State the dates you used and whether you used a CRM-object lookup or text search
</usage_guidance>

objectType.description: CRM object type: CONTACT, TICKET, DEAL, or COMPANY. Required with objectId for CRM-object mode.

objectId.description: CRM object ID. Required with objectType for CRM-object mode.

startTime.description: Start of time-range search (inclusive), as an ISO-8601 string (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ) or yyyy-MM-dd (UTC midnight). Optional: omit to search from the beginning of time up to endTime. For a 'last N days' or recency search, set startTime only and omit endTime; STARTED_AT_* aggregationDimensions need both startTime and endTime. May combine with query. With STARTED_AT_* aggregationDimensions, buckets follow the portal's time zone, so for a non-UTC portal a date-only window can return partial first and last buckets.

endTime.description: End of time-range search (inclusive). Same formats as startTime; a date-only value (yyyy-MM-dd) covers the whole day through 23:59:59.999 UTC. Omit endTime to search up to now. A current time you supply can lag the server clock and cut off the latest updates. May combine with query.

messageLimit.description: Messages per conversation, oldest first. Default 100, max 200. A longer thread returns only its first messageLimit messages.

after.description: Pagination cursor for CRM-object, time-range, and no-mode requests; text search does not paginate. To get more results, pass the previous response's nextPageAfter value verbatim with the same mode and filters. A response without nextPageAfter is the last page. Never construct, increment, or guess a cursor.

inboxId.description: Inbox ID filter. Works in time-range, no-mode, aggregation, and KEYWORD text-search requests; rejected in CRM-object mode and with searchMethod SEMANTIC. In KEYWORD text search, naming an inbox makes totalConversations a distinct count for that inbox and time window. Caveat (time-range and aggregation): matches hs_inbox_id, which is under-populated on Live Chat / Email conversations — prefer channelInstanceId, or resolve all instances of an inbox via get_conversation_channel_metadata and query each.

conversationChannelId.description: Generic channel type ID for a type such as EMAIL or LIVE_CHAT. Get the numeric value from channelId in get_conversation_channel_metadata. Works in all modes. To label CHANNEL aggregation buckets, read the channelName already on each bucket.

channelInstanceId.description: Specific configured channel instance ID for an email address, WhatsApp number, or form. Get the numeric value from channelInstanceId in get_conversation_channel_metadata. Use it when the user names a specific address, number, or form. Works in all modes.

conversationStatus.description: Status filter: CONVERSATION_STATUS_OPEN or CONVERSATION_STATUS_CLOSED. Works in all modes.

assignedAgentId.description: Assigned agent filter: only return conversations assigned to this HubSpot user id (the <userId> in actor id "A-<userId>"). Use it for "my conversations" and owner scans; each result also includes assignedAgentId. To name an agent whose assignedAgentName or senderName is absent, look the id up with search_crm_objects on USER by hs_internal_user_id. Works in time-range, aggregation, and CRM-object modes. In text-search mode, applied as a post-filter after cv-search returns hits.

includedMessages.description: Which messages to return: NONE (conversation metadata only), STANDARD (human, agent and bot messages), WITH_AUTOMATED (also AI agent replies and workflow or bulk sends), or ALL (also agents' internal notes and chat greetings; ratings are never returned). Default STANDARD. When you need message content, keep the default rather than scanning then re-querying. Use NONE only for wide count/filter queries, such as an owner's conversations, to return metadata before deciding which conversations to read. To count conversations that mention something, use NONE: otherwise an empty KEYWORD search is retried as SEMANTIC and returns its nearest matches.

includeAllDialogue.description: Also return AI agent replies, workflow or bulk sends, agents' internal notes, and chat greetings. Default false returns human, agent and bot messages. Only applies with includeMessages=true; text search rejects it otherwise.

query.description: Search query for text-search mode. Searches message bodies. searchMethod selects how it matches: KEYWORD does literal terms and is the default, SEMANTIC matches by meaning. Quote the whole query for an exact phrase in KEYWORD mode. No pagination. May combine with startTime/endTime to restrict results to that window. With inboxId, totalConversations counts every keyword match in that inbox and window (approximate when conversationChannelId, channelInstanceId, or conversationStatus is set) and can exceed, or be positive without, the conversations returned; without inboxId it counts only the returned page. For a cheap count with inboxId, set maxConversations low and includeMessages=false.

searchMethod.description: Text-query search method. KEYWORD (default): literal term / BM25 match. SEMANTIC: by-meaning, paraphrase, and cross-language match, ordered by relevance; requires query, allows startTime/endTime, rejects after and inboxId. An empty text search is retried once with the other method, and the response's searchMethod names the method that produced the results. SEMANTIC results match by meaning, so check them before saying a conversation mentions something.

includeMessages.description: Whether messages are included. Default true (one call returns content inline). When you need message content, keep the default rather than scanning then re-querying. Set false only for wide count/filter queries, such as an owner's conversations, to return metadata (conversationId, threadId, timestamps) before deciding which conversations to read. To count conversations that mention something, set false: with true, an empty KEYWORD search is retried as SEMANTIC and returns its nearest matches.

messageDetail.description: Per-message shape. TEXT_ONLY, WITH_ROLE, FULL. TEXT_ONLY = messageId+text+createdAt+messageType, for when speaker roles don't matter. WITH_ROLE (default, fits most summaries) adds derived actorType (e.g. AGENT, VISITOR, SYSTEM) and senderContactId. FULL adds senders/recipients/channel metadata and each message's senderName and sender actorId (messageSenders[].actorId): "A-<userId>" for an agent, where userId is the HubSpot user id (not a contact id or hubspot_owner_id), and "V-<contactId>" for a visitor. Pass FULL only when you need per-sender detail; at max page volume FULL responses can exceed MCP-client size caps. Ignored when includeMessages=false or in aggregation mode.

aggregationDimensions.description: Aggregation mode dimensions: STATUS, CHANNEL, STARTED_AT_DAY, STARTED_AT_WEEK. Pass several dimensions in a SINGLE call to get multiple breakdowns at once (e.g. [STATUS, CHANNEL] returns one independent bucket list per dimension, not a crosstab); do not make a separate call per dimension. STARTED_AT_* requires startTime+endTime. STARTED_AT_DAY and STARTED_AT_WEEK are mutually exclusive — at most one date-histogram dimension per call. Aggregation counts conversations started in the window (hs_started_at); time-range search instead returns conversations active in the window (hs_lastmodifieddate). Empty (default) = non-aggregation mode.

maxBucketsPerDimension.description: Max buckets per dimension. Default 90, max 100. For date histograms, a request is rejected when the number of calendar buckets it spans exceeds min(this, 90) in both UTC and the portal's time zone, so a non-UTC portal can receive one extra partial bucket.

tools.name: get_user_details
tools.description:
Returns the current user's identity and hub info, plus optional team and role context.

Call this before other HubSpot operations to establish the current user's identity. Returns info for the current user only — to find other users/owners, search the "users" objectType with search_crm_objects.

<usage_guidance>
- To check which object types the user can read or write, use discover_hubspot_schema. TOOL_INFORMATION is deprecated; do not request it or rely on it.
- `include` selects sections; TEAMS_AND_ROLES must be requested explicitly.
- TEAMS_AND_ROLES is personal context only (the user's primary team with member owner IDs, job title, seats, direct report owner IDs). For org-wide teams/roles, "my teams", or account settings (timezone, currency, account type), use get_organization_details.
- directReports are NOT team members. If the user asks about direct reports and directReports is empty, tell them none are configured and ask before substituting team members — never substitute automatically.
</usage_guidance>

Returns:
- userId and hubId (accountId)
- `guidance` (if present): relay its message to the user
- `onboarded` (if present): false = portal has not completed initial setup
- `userDefaultBrand` (if present): the user's default brand (id, name); refer to it by name when responding to the user. Absent if they default to all brands or brands are unavailable.

include.description:
Optional list of data sections to include in the user details response.
Available values:
- USER_INFORMATION: The current user's personal details (owner ID, name, email)
- TEAMS_AND_ROLES: The user's team memberships and role assignments
- TOOL_INFORMATION: Deprecated. Use discover_hubspot_schema for object type read/write access.

If not specified or empty, the USER_INFORMATION section is returned.
Specify only the sections you need to reduce response size.
Unrecognized values are ignored.

tools.name: search_crm_objects
tools.description:
Searches and retrieves CRM records from HubSpot by filters, associations, and criteria. Returns actual records, not field definitions (use search_properties to discover fields, discover_hubspot_schema to discover object types).

Returns: id, requested properties, urlTemplate, total (match count for analytics/pagination), offset.

Rules:
- objectType MUST be an exact type identifier. Standard types (CONTACT, DEAL) work directly; for any concept noun ("lead", "appointment", "account"), ALWAYS call discover_hubspot_schema for its typeName — never infer from training data, as schemas are portal-specific (e.g. "lead" may be a LEAD or a CONTACT lifecycle stage). Re-resolve if results are empty/unexpected.
- To learn a type's data model or recover from 0 results, sample via get_crm_objects (no properties) and confirm values with search_properties before refining filters.
- Max 5 filterGroups, up to 6 filters each, 18 total.
- Always check total; never substitute sample/partial data for actual data.
- Prefer this tool for record retrieval; for complex analysis, refine requirements with the user and segment large datasets.
- You MUST return a clickable URL (from urlTemplate, with UTM params) for every record.
- Use associatedWith to filter/list objects by association; use search_owners to list users/owners.
- First-person queries ("my deals", "contacts I own") MUST filter hubspot_owner_id = {ownerId} from get_user_details; fetching ownerId without applying it returns all records, not the user's.
- Currency: when returning a currency amount (DEAL.amount, LINE_ITEM.price, QUOTE.hs_quote_amount, INVOICE.hs_amount_billed, CART/ORDER.hs_total_price, SUBSCRIPTION.hs_mrr, COMMERCE_PAYMENT.hs_initial_amount) also request its currency-code property (DEAL: deal_currency_code; LINE_ITEM: hs_line_item_currency_code; QUOTE/INVOICE: hs_currency; else hs_currency_code). For DEAL aggregation use amount_in_home_currency (never pair with deal_currency_code); never sum raw amount across differing currencies.

objectType.description:
Mandatory field specifying the ObjectType to search for objects for.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, and other documented HubSpot objects) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` (e.g. `p885186001_fleet_vehicles`) that you MUST obtain from `discover_hubspot_schema` before searching — do not construct or guess it.
A plausible standard-looking name (e.g. `products`) may actually resolve to a different standard object OR a custom object. When you are not certain a name is a standard type, treat it as non-standard and resolve it via `discover_hubspot_schema` first, then use the exact `typeName` it returns.

query.description:
Optional text to search for within the default searchable properties of the specified object type.
Uses simple text matching (contains)
Each object type has different searchable properties.
contacts - firstname, lastname, email, phone, company),
companies - name, website, domain, phone),
deals - dealname, pipeline, dealstage, description, dealtype)
ticket - subject, content, hs_pipeline_stage, hs_ticket_category, hs_ticket_id)

[Important] Common stop words (e.g., "the", "a", "of", "and", "in") may not be indexed for some object types. If a query returns no results, retry by removing stop words or using property filters instead of free-text search.

Max length - 200 chars

properties.description: Optional list of property names to include in results. Returns default set if empty. Specify the minimum set of properties needed for the task for best results. Leave it empty only if you explicitly need to discover the full default property set.

propertyName.description: The name of the property to sort by

sorts.description: Optional sorting rules for results. Only one sort rule can be applied

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page. Max: 200, Default: 100

propertyName.description:
Specify the name of the Crm Object Property to filter on.

DO NOT use the pseudo-property `associations.{objectType}` or `associated_{objectType}` for associations.

You can use the following properties to filter by the number of associated records:

Tickets - hs_num_associated_companies
Companies - num_associated_contacts, num_associated_deals
Contacts - num_associated_deals
Deals - num_associated_contacts

operator.description:
Filter operator:
  EQ, NEQ, LT, LTE, GT, GTE, BETWEEN, IN, NOT_IN, HAS_PROPERTY, NOT_HAS_PROPERTY, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN
Usage:
  No additional parameters required for HAS_PROPERTY and NOT_HAS_PROPERTY

value.description: Value parameter for single-value operators (EQ, NEQ, LT, LTE, GT, GTE, CONTAINS_TOKEN, NOT_CONTAINS_TOKEN)

highValue.description: High value for range-based operators like BETWEEN

values.description: Set of values for multi-value operators like IN and NOT_IN

items.description:
Represents a filter condition for CRM object searches.
 Filters specify criteria that property values must meet to be included in search results.
 The available operators are defined in {@link PropertyFilterOperator}.

filters.description: Set of filters in this group. All filters combined with logical ANDThe filter is used with associatedWith for AND logic in the same FilterGroup.

objectType.description:
Object type to find associations with.

Example: "companies" to find records associated with a company

operator.description:
Operator for association filtering:
- EQUAL/NOT_EQUAL: Associated with the specified object.
- IN/NOT_IN: Associated with any of the specified objects.

objectIds.description:
DEPRECATED: Use objectIdValues instead.
List of object IDs as strings to filter by.
If both objectIds and objectIdValues are provided, objectIdValues takes precedence.
Valid IDs are string representations of positive longs (e.g., '123', '456').

For EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators, provide exactly one ID eg. ["123"]
For IN and NOT_IN operators, provide multiple IDs eg. ["123", "456", "789"]

objectIdValues.description:
List of object IDs to filter by.

At least one valid object ID must be provided.
Each object ID greater than 0.
Maximum of 100 object IDs allowed per association filter.

For EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators, provide exactly one ID eg. [123]
For IN and NOT_IN operators, provide multiple IDs eg. [123, 456, 789]

associatedWith.description:
Association filters for finding records related to specific objects (e.g., "contacts for company X").

Within a single FilterGroup, all association filters are combined with AND logic.
Association filters are also ANDed with any property filters in the same FilterGroup.

Examples:
- Find contacts associated with company 123:
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [123]}]

- Find contacts associated with company 123 OR 456 (use IN operator):
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "IN", "objectIdValues": [123, 456]}]

- Find records associated with BOTH company 123 AND contact 456 (multiple filters):
  [{"objectType": "companies", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [123]},
   {"objectType": "contacts", "operator": "EQUAL", "objectIdValues": [456]}]

- To search for company A OR company B, use separate FilterGroups (FilterGroups are ORed together).

items.description:
Represents a group of filters that are logically connected with AND operators.
 Multiple filter groups in a search request are combined with OR operators.

filterGroups.description:
* The filter groups that define the search criteria.
 * Filters that match ALL of several conditions (AND logic) should be put in the same filterGroup.
 * Filters that match AT LEAST ONE of several conditions (OR logic) should be put in a separate filterGroup.

userIntent.description:
The original intent or goal the user was trying to accomplish.
Set to "<unchanged>" if the intent has already been submitted and hasn't changed.
Use generic or anonymized references instead of specific names, emails, or other PII.
Replace specific names with generalized references:
- Company/Partner names: "Bluleadz partner" → "partner A"
- Deal names: "Tesla deal" → "deal A"
- Customer names: "Acme Corp customer" → "company X"
Important: Avoid adding extraneous information other than what the user provides in the current chat.
Maximum 40 words.

satisfaction.description:
The user's satisfaction during the conversation.
  Set to DISSATISFIED when the user struggled with a feature, mentioned an unmet need or showed dissatisfaction.
  <dissatisfied_signals>
  - User provides explicit correction: "No, I meant...", "Actually, I want..."
  - User repeats query with different phrasing
  - User states something is wrong: "That's wrong", "That's not right"
  - User clarifies because agent misunderstood
  </dissatisfied_signals>
  Set to SATISFIED when the user expresses satisfaction, gratitude, or approval.
  Set to NEUTRAL when the conversation flowed smoothly without strong emotional signals.

chatInsights.description:
Insights about the chat including user intent and satisfaction level.
IMPORTANT: MUST be provided for all scenarios.

tools.name: manage_crm_objects
tools.description:
Creates or updates CRM objects and their associations. Use createRequest to create objects; use updateRequest to update existing objects or associate two existing objects. For any association or association-label work, first call the `tool_guidance` tool for `manage_crm_objects` — detailed association steps live there.

<required_first_step>
BEFORE proposing or making any change, call discover_hubspot_schema (GET_OBJECT_TYPES for the target objectType) and check its writeAccess. If writeAccess is not AVAILABLE (e.g. REQUIRES_PERMISSION_MODIFICATION), do NOT show a confirmation table and do NOT call this tool — explain the limitation to the user and stop.
</required_first_step>

<mandatory_confirmation>
Before every create or update, show the proposed changes in a table (columns: Object Type | ID | Property | Current Value | New Value) and get explicit user approval. This is CRITICAL.
- Use human-friendly property labels ("Deal Stage", not "dealstage") and enum display labels ("Closed Won", not "closedwon"); if you lack label info from a prior call, fetch it with search_properties first.
- End with an approval prompt, e.g. "Approve? [✅ Yes / ❌ No]".
- On the FIRST confirmation only, also add: "Want to skip confirmations for this chat? Just ask." Then stop offering it but keep confirming. If the user opts out, skip confirmations for the session.
</mandatory_confirmation>

<guidance>
- Limit to a MAXIMUM of 10 objects per request (upserts and associations).
- Not all properties are editable. Use search_properties to list properties, or search_crm_objects to sample data, before changes.
- hubspot_owner_id defaults to the current user when omitted; set it to empty string to leave unowned.
- For concept nouns ("lead", "appointment", "account"), ALWAYS call discover_hubspot_schema first for the exact typeName — never infer from training data; schemas are portal-specific (e.g. "lead" may be LEAD or a CONTACT lifecycle stage), and creating the wrong object type cannot be undone.
</guidance>

objectType.description: The object type to create (e.g., contacts, companies, deals, tickets)

properties.description: The property keys and associated values for each key to set on the newly created object

associations.description:
Optional list of associations to create with this object.
For CREATE operations, associations are created after the object is successfully created.
Each association requires a target object ID & target object type.

objects.description: A list of CRM objects to create

createRequest.description: Required when creating new CRM objects.

objectType.description: The object type to update (e.g., contacts, companies, deals, tickets)

objectId.description: The ID of the object to update

properties.description: The property keys and values to update on the existing object. Leave empty to only create associations

associations.description:
Optional list of associations to create with this object.
For UPDATE operations, associations are created after the object is successfully updated.
Each association requires a target object ID and target object type.

objects.description: A list of CRM objects to update

updateRequest.description: Required when updating existing CRM objects.

confirmationStatus.description: Indicates whether the user has approved this action. Must be CONFIRMED or CONFIRMATION_WAIVED_FOR_SESSION before invoking the tool.

targetObjectId.description: The ID of the target object to associate with

targetObjectType.description: The object type of the target object (e.g., CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL)

labels.description:
List of association label names to add to this association.
Labels must already exist for the object type pair (e.g., "Contact with Primary Company", "Billing Contact").
Specified labels are added to any existing labels on the association.
If not specified, only the default association is created/updated and existing labels are left unchanged.

tools.name: get_marketing_email_analytics
tools.description:
Provides analytics data for marketing emails based on sends in the given date range. To find emails created or published within certain date ranges, use search_crm_objects instead.

The request takes a single field, analysisRequest, which is an OBJECT — never a bare string. It carries a "_type" discriminator plus the section settings for that type. 
Available analysisRequest types (set as analysisRequest._type):
- "OVERVIEW" — portal-level aggregate statistics (sends, deliveries, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes)   over a date range, optionally scoped to specific emails or broken down by time interval.   Uses statisticsSection.
- "HEALTH" — portal email health diagnostics. Four sections:   mxGroupStatisticsSection (delivery performance statistics by the destination domains with the most deliveries, over a date range);   healthScoresSection (monthly 0–100 health scores with per-metric breakdown for   click, open, hard bounce, spam report, unsubscribe, and click-to-open — up to 6 months,   GLOBAL or INDUSTRY benchmark);   sourceHealthScoresSection (same per-metric breakdown per contact source, i.e.   where contacts were imported from, past ~30 days);   bounceReasonsSection (breakdown of bounces by reason category over a date range,   split into hard and soft bounces, optionally scoped to a single MX group).
- "RECIPIENTS" — delivery outcome and engagement summary for a specific contact recipient,   with an optional ordered event timeline (sent, opened, clicked, bounced, etc.).   Uses recipientDetailsSection.   No operation returns a collection of all recipients for an email;   only individual recipient information is available.
- "UNSUBSCRIBE_SURVEY" — breakdown of unsubscribe survey responses by reason code   (NO_LONGER_INTERESTED, DID_NOT_SIGN_UP, TOO_MANY_EMAILS, IRRELEVANT_CONTENT, OTHER)   over a date range. Optionally scoped to a specific email by emailContentId.   Use this to understand WHY contacts unsubscribed and improve future emails.

analysisRequest.description: The analysis request object. Set '_type' to 'OVERVIEW', 'HEALTH', or 'RECIPIENTS' and include the corresponding section settings.

mode.description: Deprecated alias for analysisRequest; use analysisRequest instead.

_type.description: Email health diagnostics. Supports portal-level health scores, deliverability stats per MX group, and health scores per contact source.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

frequency.description: Aggregation for the results. Use TOTAL to return a single aggregated value for the full date range. Use DAILY, WEEKLY, or MONTHLY to return a time series broken down by that interval. Defaults to MONTHLY.

limit.description: Maximum number of top MX groups to return when no MX group filter is provided. Defaults to 10.

mxGroups.description: MX groups to filter by (e.g. "gmail.com", "outlook.com"). If empty, the top N groups by delivered volume are used.

emailType.description: Restrict results to emails of this type. Omit to include all email types.

marketingEmailObjectIds.description: Restrict results to these marketing email object IDs (hs_object_id on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object, returned as a String by CRM search tools — cast to Long before passing here).

filters.description: Filters to restrict which data is included in the results.

mxGroupStatisticsSection.description: MX group statistics section. Provide to query performance statistics broken down by the destination domains with the most deliveries.

scoreType.description: Whether to evaluate scores against global absolute thresholds (GLOBAL) or against industry benchmarks (INDUSTRY). Defaults to GLOBAL.

numberOfMonths.description: Number of months of history to return, counting back from the current month (inclusive). Must be between 1 and 6. Defaults to 6.

healthScoresSection.description: Health scores section. Provide to query monthly portal health scores for a configurable number of months, including per-metric breakdown.

sourceHealthScoresSection.description: Source health scores section. Provide to query health scores broken down by contact source (where contacts were imported from). Covers the service-configured window, currently 30 days.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd. The date range must not exceed six months.

mxGroup.description: Restrict the breakdown to a single MX group (e.g. "gmail.com", "outlook.com"). Omit to include bounces across all MX groups.

bounceReasonsSection.description: Bounce reasons section. Provide to query a breakdown of bounces by reason category, split into hard and soft bounces, for the portal.

_type.description: Recipient-level data for a specific contact that received a marketing email.

marketingEmailObjectId.description: Required. The marketing email object ID — the hs_object_id property on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object, returned as a String by CRM search tools. Cast to Long before passing here.

contactCrmObjectId.description: Required. The CONTACT CRM object ID of the recipient to look up.

includeEvents.description: When true, fetches the full ordered event timeline for this recipient (sent, opened, clicked, bounced, etc.). Defaults to false to avoid the extra round-trip when only the delivery summary is needed.

recipientDetailsSection.description: Recipient details section: delivery outcome, engagement summary, and optional event timeline for a specific contact.

_type.description: Breakdown of unsubscribe survey responses by reason code over a date range.

startDate.description: Required. Start of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

endDate.description: Required. End of the reporting period (inclusive). Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

emailContentId.description: Optional. Marketing email content ID (hs_object_id on MARKETING_EMAIL, cast from String to Long). When provided, returns survey responses scoped to sends of this specific email. When omitted, returns portal-wide aggregate data.

includeOtherTexts.description: When true, the response includes the raw free-text entries submitted by contacts who selected 'Other' as their reason. Use this when you intend to summarize or analyze the verbatim feedback. Defaults to false.

_type.description: Portal-level aggregate send statistics broken down over a date range.

marketingEmailObjectIds.description: Restrict results to these marketing email object IDs (hs_object_id on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object, returned as a String by CRM search tools — cast to Long before passing here).

tools.name: search_owners
tools.description:
Lists and searches for owners who can be assigned to CRM records.

<capabilities>
- Supports searching by name/email or batch lookup by owner IDs
- HubSpot owner ids and user IDs are distinct, lookups only work when owner ids are provided specifically
</capabilities>

tools.name: manage_marketing_email
tools.description:
Manages a marketing email's settings and content. Call tool_guidance for guidance.

Settings sub-operations (_type):
- "LIST_SUBSCRIPTION_TYPES" — list subscription types;   call before CREATE to get a valid subscriptionTypeId
- "LIST_FROM_ADDRESSES" — list verified from addresses;   call before CREATE to choose a replyToEmail;   if address not listed, list options and stop
- "CREATE" — create a new email   (required: name, subject, fromName, replyToEmail, subscriptionTypeId;   permanent fields — ask the user BEFORE calling CREATE:   templatePath: ask template or blank? call LIST_TEMPLATES to show options;   brandId; emailType: BATCH by default, AUTOMATED for workflow emails)
- "POLL_EMAIL_CREATION" — poll for CRM object; takes marketingEmailId
- "UPDATE" — update email settings;   template/brandId cannot be changed after creation
- "CLONE" — clone into a new draft
- "GET_EMAIL_DETAILS" — retrieve current settings
- "GET_TEMPLATE" — retrieve a template by path
- "LIST_TEMPLATES" — search/browse templates by kind   (CODED or DND) and filename

Content sub-operations (marketingEmailObjectId):
- "GET_CONTENT" — returns the editable layout
- "EDIT_CONTENT" — always call tool_guidance; resubmit   full layout; preserve all styling, only change text/links/images
- "PREVIEW_CONTENT" — renders the email; returns   subjectLine, renderedText, (optional) renderedHtml
- "AB_TEST_EMAIL" — set up an A/B test on a draft email by adding Version B;   use this whenever the user asks to test two versions, create a version B, split test,   or try two subject lines — they often don't say "A/B" explicitly

Only draft emails can be edited. Always show proposed changes and get explicit user confirmation before creating, updating, or editing.

name.description: Required. Internal name for the email (e.g., 'Spring Sale 2026').

fromName.description: Required. The sender's display name (e.g., 'Marketing Team').

subscriptionTypeId.description: Required. The subscription type ID. Determines which contacts are eligible.

brandId.description: The brand ID (also called business unit ID). Required for portals with multiple brands. Cannot be changed after creation — ask the user before creating.

exclusionListIds.description: Contact list IDs to exclude (suppression lists).

includeContactIds.description: Individual contact VIDs to include as recipients. Use instead of or alongside includeListIds.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: The CRM object ID of the CAMPAIGN to associate with this email.

templatePath.description: Template path from LIST_TEMPLATES. Omit for a blank email. Cannot be changed after creation.

previewText.description: Preview text shown in email clients before the message is opened (typically 50–100 chars).

emailType.description: The type of email to create. BATCH (default) for marketing blasts sent to contact lists at a scheduled time. AUTOMATED for workflow-triggered emails — recipients are enrolled via workflows, not contact lists. Cannot be changed via these tools after creation — if a change is needed, the user must update it in the HubSpot UI before publishing.

marketingEmailObjectId.description: The marketing email object ID (hs_object_id on the MARKETING_EMAIL CRM object). Required.

subscriptionTypeId.description: The subscription type ID. Determines which contacts are eligible.

includeListIds.description: Contact list IDs to include as recipients.

exclusionListIds.description: Contact list IDs to exclude (suppression lists).

includeContactIds.description: Individual contact VIDs to include as recipients. Use instead of or alongside includeListIds.

campaignCrmObjectId.description: The CRM object ID of the CAMPAIGN to associate with this email.

tools.name: query_crm_data
tools.description:
Queries HubSpot CRM data via SQL with HubSpot-specific extensions.
IMPORTANT: You MUST call the Tool Guidance tool before your first query. It contains required guidance and examples.

<select>
IMPORTANT: Property names must exactly match HubSpot internal names. Always call search_properties to confirm names before querying.
The record identifier property is hs_object_id.
For financial values, prefer properties ending in _in_home_currency.
  <unsupported>SELECT DISTINCT, AS aliases, CASE WHEN, IF(), string functions (CONCAT, UPPER, etc.), COALESCE, associations.OBJECT.</unsupported>
</select>

<from>
One object type per query: CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET, etc. Use a user-details tool to discover supported types.
  <unsupported>JOIN, UNION, subqueries, CTEs.</unsupported>
</from>

<where>
Operators — comparison: =, !=, <, >, <=, >=; text/substring match: column LIKE '%value%'; presence: column IS NULL / column IS NOT NULL.
List membership: hs_crm_search.ilsListIds = 'LIST_ID' (cannot combine with aggregates or GROUP BY).
Date filters: in an aggregation (GROUP BY or aggregate) use a YYYY-MM-DD date, matched by day; in a plain row SELECT either a date or a full timestamp (e.g. '2025-01-01 14:00:00') works.
"My"/"I" queries: filter by hubspot_owner_id (see Tool Guidance for resolution steps).
</where>

<group-by>
DATE_TRUNC(prop, 'INTERVAL') — INTERVAL: DAY | WEEK | MONTH | QUARTER | YEAR.
MEDIAN(prop) supported alongside standard aggregates.
  <unsupported>HAVING.</unsupported>
</group-by>

<order-by>
Sort direction: ORDER BY column ASC for ascending, DESC for descending.
</order-by>

<cross-object>
To retrieve associated object data, use OBJECT.property (e.g., SELECT COMPANY.name FROM CONTACT) — NOT associations.OBJECT.
associations.OBJECT is for WHERE existence checks only (IS NULL / IS NOT NULL). Never use it in SELECT or GROUP BY.
A query can reference at most 2 different associated object types.
</cross-object>

tools.name: manage_aeo_prompts
tools.description:
Read AI responses to tracked prompts, or create and run new tracked prompts.
Provide exactly one `operation`, a JSON object (not a string) with an
`_operationType` field set to DETAIL (a single prompt's per-run summaries —
assistant, model, mention and citation counts, cited URLs — for an assistant and
date window, without response text), RESPONSES (the full AI response text of up to
5 runs, by promptId or runUuids), or CREATE (start tracking new prompts and run
them immediately). CREATE requires a
confirmed=false preview before confirmed=true. Call get_aeo_metrics with
include=["BUSINESS_UNITS"] then include=["ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS"] to get the
businessUnitId, icpIds, and productIds that CREATE needs. Call tool_guidance
(mcpToolInstructions) for the confirmation workflow and per-operation details.

promptId.description: Prompt record ID to drill into. Discover it from get_aeo_metrics include=["PROMPTS"].

startDate.description: ISO-8601 start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to 30 days ago. Per-run results on or after this date are returned.

endDate.description: ISO-8601 end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to today. Must be on or after startDate.

aiAssistant.description: AI assistant family to filter runs by (CHATGPT, GEMINI, CLAUDE, PERPLEXITY). Omit to return runs for all assistants.

maxRuns.description: Maximum number of run summaries to include. Defaults to 10; capped at 25.

businessUnitId.description: Business unit ID. Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["BUSINESS_UNITS"] to discover available business units and their IDs. The business unit must already have an input profile.

promptTexts.description: Optional, for the MANUAL path only: exact prompt texts the user dictated, e.g. "What is the best CRM for small businesses?". Each entry must be a single line of text with no line breaks — submit multi-line input as separate entries. Leave EMPTY to have AEO generate the prompts from the icpIds, productIds, and buyingJourneyPhases below (the recommended path) — do not write prompts yourself. In the generated flow the first confirmed=false call starts generation and returns a previewToken; call confirmed=false again with that previewToken until the generated prompts come back, then confirm by passing the previewToken on a confirmed=true call (not the texts).

previewToken.description: The token returned when a confirmed=false call starts AEO generation. Pass it back on subsequent confirmed=false calls to poll for the generated prompts, then on the confirmed=true call (leaving promptTexts empty) to persist the exact prompts AEO generated, each bound to its own ICP, product, and buying-journey phase. Not used for the manual promptTexts path.

buyingJourneyPhases.description: Optional buying-journey phases to generate prompts for (AWARENESS, CONSIDERATION, EVALUATION, DECISION). Used only when promptTexts is empty. Defaults to CONSIDERATION.

numberOfPrompts.description: Optional number of prompts to generate per ICP x product x phase combination (minimum 1). Used only when promptTexts is empty. Defaults to 1.

icpIds.description: ICP IDs to associate with the new prompts. Required. Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS"] to discover valid IDs.

productIds.description: Product IDs to associate with the new prompts. Required. Call get_aeo_metrics with include=["ICPS_AND_PRODUCTS"] to discover valid IDs.

topicIds.description: Optional topic IDs to associate with the new prompts.

previewOffset.description: For paging through a large AEO-generated preview: the 0-based index of the first generated prompt to return. Used only with previewToken on confirmed=false calls. Defaults to 0. Pass the response's nextPreviewOffset back here to see the next page; confirming tracks the full generated set regardless of paging.

confirmed.description: Set to true only after showing the user the preview response and receiving explicit approval. First call must use confirmed=false to get a preview.

creditsAcknowledged.description: Required to be true for accounts billed in HubSpot Credits before any prompts are created. Set true ONLY after relaying the CREATE preview's credit notice (shown when onCredits is true) to the user and receiving explicit approval to incur the cost. Ignored for accounts not billed in credits.

promptId.description: Prompt record ID whose AI responses to return. Discover it from get_aeo_metrics include=["PROMPTS"].

runUuids.description: Specific runs to return, by runUuid from a DETAIL response's runSummaries (at most 5). Omit to return the prompt's latest runs instead.

aiAssistant.description: AI assistant family to filter the latest runs by (CHATGPT, GEMINI, CLAUDE, PERPLEXITY). Omit to include all assistants. Ignored when runUuids is set.

startDate.description: ISO-8601 start date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the latest runs. Optional; defaults to 30 days ago. Ignored when runUuids is set.

endDate.description: ISO-8601 end date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the latest runs. Optional; defaults to today. Ignored when runUuids is set.

maxRuns.description: Number of latest runs to return when runUuids is omitted. Defaults to 3; capped at 5.

The object must include an "_operationType" field set to exactly one of "DETAIL" or "CREATE", alongside that operation's own fields. Use DETAIL to drill into a single tracked prompt's run history, or CREATE to create and run new tracked prompts. Provide exactly one operation. Example: {"_operationType": "CREATE", "businessUnitId": 123, "promptTexts": ["What is the best CRM for small businesses?"], "icpIds": [1], "productIds": [2]}.

tools.name: read_campaign_data
tools.description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP: before your first call, invoke tool_guidance for "read_campaign_data" and follow it; it contains the required parameter details and examples for each operation. Reads campaign data using one of four operations selected by the `operation` field. GET_ANALYTICS: engagement metrics (sessions, new contacts, influenced contacts) for one or more campaigns. GET_ASSET_METRICS: performance metrics for assets of one type associated with a campaign. Metrics are type-specific and NOT comparable across types — do NOT use this for cross-type "top/best performing asset" questions; use getCampaignAttributionReports with dimension=ASSET_TITLE for that (its attribution metrics share a common unit across all asset types; set sortByMetric to the metric the question asks about — REVENUE when no metric is specified). For the deals associated with a campaign (any stage, regardless of close date), use GET_ASSET_METRICS with assetType=DEAL (preferred); search_crm_objects is a less reliable route that can return incomplete or incorrect results, so only fall back to it if GET_ASSET_METRICS fails. Do NOT use GET_ASSET_METRICS for deals closed or won in a period or their deal values: use getCampaignAttributionReports with DEAL_NAME and DEAL_AMOUNT for that. GET_CONTACTS: paginated contact IDs attributed to a campaign, filtered by attribution type (NEW_CONTACTS_FIRST_TOUCH, NEW_CONTACTS_LAST_TOUCH, INFLUENCED_CONTACTS). GET_CAMPAIGN_ASSET_TYPES: returns the portal-enabled campaign asset types with human-readable aliases (e.g. AUTOMATION_PLATFORM_FLOW → workflows). No additional request parameters needed.

tools.name: get_organization_details
tools.description:
Get organization-wide teams, job titles (roles), seats, account info (timezone, currency, account type, portal name), and brands. Use the include parameter (TEAMS, SEATS, JOB_TITLES, ACCOUNT_INFORMATION, BRANDS) to fetch only what you need.

Returns only the included sections (or all if include is omitted):
- TEAMS: teams with name and member owner IDs (org-wide, not personal).
- SEATS: available seat type NAMES only, not user counts.
- JOB_TITLES: roles/job titles present in the org.
- ACCOUNT_INFORMATION: timezone, currency, account type, UI domain, account ID, portal name, create date.
- BRANDS: the account's brands and the primary brand, each with id and name. Brand IDs are the values of the CRM property hs_all_assigned_business_unit_ids; use them only in tool calls and refer to brands by name when responding to the user. (The current user's own default brand is on get_user_details.)
- guidance (optional): if present, read it carefully; it may hold a user-facing message (e.g. missing permissions to relay) or an internal hint (e.g. name disambiguation).

Routing:
- First-person personal context ("my team", "my role", "my manager", "my direct reports") -> use get_user_details instead.
- EXCEPTION: plural "my teams" / "which teams am I on" -> use THIS tool (get_user_details returns only one primaryTeam).
- Org-wide references ("our sales team", "the marketing team", "all managers") -> use this tool.

Follow-ups (this tool alone does not count or list users/deals):
- Count users by seat or role: get seat type names / job titles here, then filter search_crm_objects on the USER objectType by each. SEATS gives names only, so you MUST follow up with search_crm_objects for per-seat counts.
- A team's data ("our sales team's deals"): include=[TEAMS] to resolve members to owner IDs, then pass those IDs as filters to search_crm_objects.
- Which teams a user is on: include=[TEAMS], then match the user's ownerId against team member ownerIds; match on ownerId ONLY, never on member name.

include.description:
Optional list of data to include in the response.
Available values:
- TEAMS: Include the list of teams and their members
- SEATS: Include the list of seat/role names available in the account
- JOB_TITLES: Include the list of job titles assigned to users in the account
- ACCOUNT_INFORMATION: Include account details such as timezone, currency, and account type
- BRANDS: Include the account's brands and the primary brand, each with ID and name

If not specified or empty, all data will be returned.
Specify only the values you need to reduce response size.
Unrecognized values will result in an error.

Also assesses CRM onboarding status and guides the next step.</purpose><usage_guidance>For those connection checks, call this tool right away, without asking first, whatever get_user_details returned for onboarded. Otherwise, call it when get_user_details returns onboarded: false, after answering the user's question and offering to help them get started; do not call it when onboarded: true. Use action to control behavior: leave empty (the default) to just check status. SET_GOAL — records the user's primary goal; requires goal to be set to one of organizeAndTrackContacts, automateMarketing, generateLeads, manageSalesPipeline, customerSupport, billsAndCollectPayment, buildWebsite, createMarketingContent, or stillExploring — map the user's own words to the closest matching value. tools.name: search_properties
tools.description:
Finds the most relevant CRM property definitions using keyword-based search.

<capabilities>
- Lists all property definitions for an object type when no search terms are provided
- To search for actual record data, use search_crm_objects
</capabilities>

<returns>
A filtered list of matching properties, each with:
- name: Property identifier
- label: Display label
- description: Property description
- matchScore: Relevance score for the query (absent when no query is provided)
</returns>

<usage_guidance>
- Prefer the keywords field to pass multiple property-name guesses in a SINGLE request (best performance); use the query field for a single guess (backward compatibility)
- Keywords must be property-name guesses (e.g. "assignee", "zip_code"), NOT natural-language phrases
- MAXIMUM 5 keywords per request; exceeding this returns a validation error
- Omit search terms to return ALL properties for the object type (useful for discovery)
</usage_guidance>

<examples>
- "open tickets grouped by urgency" -> {"objectType": "TICKET", "keywords": ["urgency"]}
- "calls assigned to me" -> {"objectType": "CALL", "keywords": ["assignee", "assigned_to", "call_owner", "owned_by"]}
- "companies by name, employee count, zip, last contact" -> {"objectType": "COMPANY", "keywords": ["name", "employees", "zip_code", "last_contact"]}
- "analyze all tickets (property discovery)" -> {"objectType": "TICKET"}
</examples>

objectType.description: The name of the object type to search properties for

query.description:
DEPRECATED: Use keywords instead.
Single search keyword for backward compatibility.
If both query and keywords are provided, keywords takes precedence.
If empty and no keywords provided, returns all properties for the object type.

keywords.description:
Multiple search keywords (max 5) to find relevant properties using efficient keyword-based search.
Supports searching for multiple related property concepts in a single request.

Examples:
- ["urgency"] - Single keyword search
- ["assignee", "assigned_to", "owner"] - Multiple related keywords for assignment
- ["name", "employees", "zip", "contact"] - Multiple unrelated keywords for different properties

If both query and keywords are provided, keywords takes precedence.
If empty and no query provided, returns all properties for the object type.

tools.name: query_segments
tools.description:
Read-only lookups that support the manageSegment write operations. Set operation.type to:
- SearchSegmentsQuery: find existing segments by name (optionally scoped to an object type or   list type) to get the list ID needed for AddMembersOperation, RemoveMembersOperation, or a   future update/delete. With deleted=true it searches only deleted segments, to find the list   ID for a RestoreSegmentOperation.
- SearchFilterInputsQuery: resolve the ids that filter expressions take as arguments —   association type ids for ASSOCIATION(...), event type ids and properties for   UNIFIED_EVENTS(...), form guids, workflow/import ids, and marketing email triples. Users do   not know these ids; look them up here rather than guessing, because a guessed id creates a   segment that silently filters on the wrong thing. Each result includes a ready-to-use filter   fragment.
- GetSegmentQuery: fetch one segment's definition by list ID — its object type, list type,   name, description, saved filter expression, exclusions, and access level. Use it to inspect a   segment before editing it, or to answer what it filters on or excludes. This returns the   definition, not the members; deleted=true reads a deleted one. With includeUsage=true it   also returns what uses the segment (other segments, workflows, emails, ads); check this   before deleting one, or when the user asks where a segment is used.
- GetSegmentMembersQuery: list the CRM records inside a segment by list ID (record ID and   display name, plus any requested properties), paginated via cursor. This is the only way to   read a segment's members: membership is not a CRM property, so a filter search cannot   reproduce it. Works for STATIC and DYNAMIC segments.
- PreviewSegmentQuery: count the records a filter matches, minus any exclusions the segment   will carry, without saving anything. Use it when the user asks how many match or wants a   size before creating; to just create a segment, skip it.

This tool only reads; it never changes the portal and needs no confirmation.

query.description: Free-text search matched against segment names. Omit to list segments.

objectType.description:
Optional ObjectType to restrict the search to segments of that type. Omit to search across all object types.

Well-known standard CRM types (e.g. CONTACT, COMPANY, DEAL, TICKET) can be used directly. Any other type is a custom object identified by a portal-prefixed ID of the form `p<portalId>_<name>` obtained from `discover_hubspot_schema`.

listType.description: Optional list type filter: DYNAMIC to only return auto-updating ("active") segments, STATIC to only return static segments. Omit to return both.

limit.description: Maximum number of segments to return.

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging when a response has hasMore = true.

deleted.description: true to search only deleted segments (the lists app's Recently deleted view), newest deletion first, to find the list ID a RestoreSegmentOperation takes. Deleted segments never appear in a normal search.

anyOf.description:
Find existing segments by name, optionally scoped to one object type or list type. Returns the
 summaries (list ID, object type, name) needed to target the other operations, e.g. the list ID
 for AddMembersOperation or a delete. With deleted, searches deleted segments instead, for the
 list ID a RestoreSegmentOperation takes.

kind.description: What to look up: ASSOCIATION for the association type ids usable in an ASSOCIATION(object = ..., association = ...) filter, EVENT for the event type ids usable in a UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = ...) filter, EVENT_PROPERTY for the properties usable inside a UNIFIED_EVENTS body, FORM for form guids (FORM_SUBMISSION), WORKFLOW for workflow ids (IN_LIST(workflow = ...)), IMPORT for import ids (IN_LIST(import = ...)), EMAIL for the marketing email triple (EMAIL_EVENT(email = ..., app = ..., level = ...)).

objectType.description: For kind ASSOCIATION (required) and kind EVENT (optional): the ObjectType of the segment whose filter you are writing — a standard name like CONTACT, or a portal-prefixed custom type from `discover_hubspot_schema`. For kind EVENT_PROPERTY (required): the event type id returned by a kind EVENT result, e.g. '4-123456'. Ignored for other kinds.

query.description: Free-text filter matched against names and labels. Omit to list everything available.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

offset.description: Number of results to skip, for paging when a response has hasMore = true.

anyOf.description:
Look up the ids that segment filter expressions take as arguments — association type ids, event
 type ids, event properties, form guids, workflow/import ids, and marketing email triples. Users
 do not know these ids, so resolve them here rather than guessing; each result includes a
 ready-to-use filter fragment to paste into a filterExpression.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment to fetch.

includeUsage.description: true to also return usedBy: what uses this segment, such as other segments' filters and exclusions, workflows, emails and ads. Set it when the user asks where a segment is used, or before deleting one, since a segment that's in use can't be deleted until those uses are removed.

deleted.description: true to read a deleted segment, for example to see its filters before restoring it with RestoreSegmentOperation. A deleted segment is otherwise reported as not found.

anyOf.description:
Fetch one segment's details by list ID: its object type, list type, name, description, the filter
 expression it is saved with, its exclusions, and who can access it. Use it to inspect a segment
 before editing it, or to answer what a segment filters on or excludes. This reports the segment's
 definition, not its members — use GetSegmentMembersQuery to list the records inside it. With
 deleted, reads a deleted segment instead, for example to see its filters before a
 RestoreSegmentOperation.

listId.description: The list ID of the segment whose member records to list.

properties.description: Optional internal CRM property names to additionally return for each member. Every member always includes its record ID and display name; these values are returned on top of that. Omit to return only the record ID and display name.

limit.description: Maximum number of members to return in this page; page through larger segments with cursor.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; to fetch the next page, pass the exact nextCursor value returned by the previous call. This is an opaque continuation token, not a number of members to skip — do not compute or increment it yourself.

anyOf.description:
List the CRM records that are members of a segment, by its list ID. This is the only way to read
 the records inside a segment: membership is not a CRM property, so a filter search cannot
 reproduce it. Works for both STATIC and DYNAMIC segments. Paginated: pass the response's
 nextCursor back as cursor to page through large segments. Returns only the records (and
 properties) the user is allowed to see, so a page can hold fewer members than limit while hasMore
 is still true; keep paging.

objectType.description: The ObjectType to count matching records for, the same value CreateDynamicSegmentOperation takes: a standard CRM type such as CONTACT or COMPANY, or a portal-prefixed custom type (`p<portalId>_<name>`) obtained from `discover_hubspot_schema`; do not guess one.

filterExpression.description:
The filter whose matching records to count: the same expression you would give CreateDynamicSegmentOperation, so the count is what that segment would hold. Required; this never counts an object type unfiltered. Do not write exclusions into this filter: to keep out another segment's members, specific records, unsubscribed or non-marketing contacts, or an email domain, pass them in this query's exclusion fields, the same ones the create operation takes, so the segment is created with them in one call. Write such a condition here (NOT IN_LIST, hs_email_optout, hs_marketable_status, an email NOT CONTAINS) only when the user asks for it as a filter, e.g. "add a filter for contacts who are not in my VIP Customers list".

    SQL-like filter expression defining segment membership.

    Property conditions compare the object's own properties and combine with AND, OR and parentheses: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, CONTAINS_ANY (...), STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, IN (...), IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, BETWEEN x AND y. Relative dates use NOW() or TODAY() with whole-day offsets only — DAYS or WEEKS, never MONTHS/QUARTERS/YEARS (write NOW() - 90 DAYS, not NOW() - 3 MONTHS). Dates compare at day granularity, and a date property never compares = or != against a relative time (use a fixed date like '2026-08-13', or a rolling window). Example: "lifecyclestage = 'customer' AND annualrevenue > 500000". Write a value's apostrophe as two single quotes — lastname = 'O''Brien' — never with a backslash, which does not escape it.

    A != or NOT IN condition matches only records that have a value for the property; records where it is empty are left out. Include them only when the user asks, by writing (p != v OR p IS NULL) — it is stored as one condition, the segments UI's "Include records where … is empty" option, so it does not multiply like other ORs. For a property of an associated record, put that pair inside the one ASSOCIATION's braces — ASSOCIATION(...) { (p != v OR p IS NULL) } — never as two ASSOCIATIONs joined by OR. Never include them by default.

    To leave out records that match any of several combinations of conditions on two or more properties ("not any of: in Boston and a Lead; in Austin and a Customer; …"): with up to three combinations, write the negation directly, NOT ((city = 'Boston' AND lifecyclestage = 'lead') OR …); it is stored as != conditions with their usual handling of records with no value, so add nothing for those. With more, that multiplies too far to store, so it needs a helper: a segment of the records the combinations describe, excluded from the new segment. An exclusion keeps every other record, including ones with no value for those properties. Before creating anything, tell the user there are too many combinations to write as one filter, so you'll build a helper segment and exclude it, and ask whether to include records with no value for those properties (if the user already said, only confirm the helper segment). To leave them out, give the new segment p IS NOT NULL for each of those properties. A NOT over one property's values stays a single NOT IN (...).

    Keep the expression small. Before it is stored it is expanded into disjunctive normal form, so every OR multiplies: OR groups of widths w1, w2, ... produce w1 x w2 x ... branches, and every ANDed condition is copied into every branch. Branches x conditions per branch is the stored filter count, and it must stay under 250. Multiply the OR widths before writing: 8 ANDed conditions with two OR groups of 5 and 10 alternatives is 50 branches and 500 filters, already rejected. Every ASSOCIATION and NOT ASSOCIATION is copied into every branch too, and a segment holds at most 60 of those copies: one beside an OR of 30 alternatives is already 30. Several values of one property are one condition and do not multiply: p IN ('a', 'b') for exact values, p CONTAINS_ANY ('a', 'b') for substrings — never an OR of p = … or of p CONTAINS …. To fit, write those as one condition, drop redundant ANDed conditions, put ORed conditions in a helper segment referenced with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or split the audience across more than one segment; never narrow, drop or truncate the user's alternatives. A number IN (...) is stored as one filter per number, so a list of record ids (hs_object_id IN (...)) counts once per id, and inside an ASSOCIATION each id is its own association copy. A few ids fit: contacts at three given companies are ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = <id>) { hs_object_id IN (101, 202, 303) }. Only when the ids would take the segment past either limit, seed them into a hand-picked static segment of their own object type with membersToAddToStaticList and reference it with IN_LIST(list = <its id>), or ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) } for associated records.

    Property names are the object type's internal CRM property names on THIS portal — look them up via your CRM property/schema tools, never guess from display labels or other portals; a name missing from the schema fails validation. Enumeration (dropdown) values must be the internal stored value, never the display label — a wrong value is NOT rejected: the segment saves and silently matches no records, so source stored values from the property definition. There is no dotted cross-object path (company.industry = '...' is invalid); conditions on a related record go inside ASSOCIATION(...) braces.

    Engagement conditions (opened, clicked, visited, submitted, last engaged) often have two valid encodings: a filter form below, or an analytics property on the object itself (recency dates, counts). When no matching filter form or event exists — or the request spans ANY asset rather than a specific one — search the object's real properties for an equivalent before reporting the condition unsupported (the look-it-up rule still applies).

    Beyond property conditions, exactly these filter forms exist; names and named arguments (name = value, never positional) are exact — no other functions or aliases. Notation: [x] is optional; a | b means exactly one. times counts occurrences (>=, <= or =); occurred bounds when (>, >=, < or <= with a date or NOW() offset); for a window between two dates give occurred twice, one lower and one upper bound, both dates: occurred >= '2025-09-01', occurred <= '2026-06-01'. Each is optional and they MAY be combined — except where a form states an EXCEPTION.
    - IN_LIST(list = 4521): member of another segment/list (id from searchSegments). The same filter keyed differently for workflows and imports: IN_LIST(workflow = '112233', [state = 'ENROLLED'|'ACTIVE'|'COMPLETED'|'GOAL']) (state defaults to ENROLLED, ever enrolled) or IN_LIST(import = '555') — no list argument in those forms.
    - FORM_SUBMISSION([form = '<guid>'], [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 90 DAYS]): submitted a form. Leave form out for any form, e.g. FORM_SUBMISSION(occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS) — one condition, never an OR of every form.
    - PAGE_VIEW(url = '<exact url>' | url_contains = '<substring>', [times >= 2 | occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]): visited a website page. EXCEPTION: at most ONE refinement — a count OR a window, never both. The product stores one page-view refinement (the lists UI disables the second field too), so "twice in the last 30 days" is not expressible: keep the refinement the request makes primary, or ask the user which to keep. Page visits are ALWAYS this form, never UNIFIED_EVENTS — an event-form page-visit segment cannot be edited in the list UI. Negate with NOT_PAGE_VIEW(...).
    - ASSOCIATION(object = '0-2', association = 1) { industry = 'SAAS' }: has an associated record matching the braces; object is the associated record's object type id, association the numeric association type id between the two types, and the braces hold conditions on the associated record's properties. An ASSOCIATION body is conjunctive; OR inside its braces is rejected, but IN (...) inside them is fine. NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { condition } means NO associated record matches the condition, and it includes records with no associated record at all — "contacts with no closed-won deal" is NOT ASSOCIATION(object = '0-3', association = 4) { dealstage = 'closedwon' }, and "companies with no deals" is NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { hs_object_id IS NOT NULL }. Its braces take exactly ONE condition written as =, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL or IN_LIST (not a date or a range). To leave out records associated with something matching several conditions at once, build a segment of those associated records first and write NOT ASSOCIATION(...) { IN_LIST(list = <its id>) }. Never move the negation inside the braces: ASSOCIATION(...) { dealstage != 'closedwon' } means "has a deal that isn't closed won", a different audience. A segment read back may carry match = 'ALL', 'ANY_INCLUDE_EMPTY' or 'ALL_INCLUDE_EMPTY' on an ASSOCIATION (all / any associated records match, including records with none); keep it as read when you edit the segment.
    - UNIFIED_EVENTS(type = '4-123456', [times >= 2], [occurred > NOW() - 30 DAYS]) { [conditions] }: performed an event. The braces hold conditions on the event's OWN properties — take their names from searchFilterInputs (kind EVENT_PROPERTY), never from the segment object's schema.
    - EMAIL_EVENT(email = '169452110', app = 113, level = 'EMAIL_API_CAMPAIGN_GROUP', event = 'OPEN', [url_contains = '<substring>'], [occurred > '2026-01-01']): engaged with one specific marketing email. event is one of OPEN, CLICK, DELIVERED, SENT, REPLIED, BOUNCE, UNSUBSCRIBED, SPAMREPORT, PRINT. email, app and level come together from ONE searchFilterInputs (kind EMAIL) row — never mix rows or invent them. url_contains is valid only with event = 'CLICK'. EXCEPTIONS: occurred takes a fixed date only (rolling NOW() windows are rejected), no times, and no NOT form. For recency across ANY email ("opened an email in the last 30 days"), use the contact's email-engagement properties (e.g. hs_email_last_open_date) instead.
    Negate any form except EMAIL_EVENT by prefixing NOT, e.g. NOT IN_LIST(list = 4521). All forms combine freely with property conditions.

    Sourcing ids — users do not know these ids; look them up, never invent one (a guessed id creates a segment that silently filters on the wrong thing): list ids from searchSegments; association type ids, event type ids, event property names, form guids, workflow ids, import ids and email triples from searchFilterInputs (kind ASSOCIATION, EVENT, EVENT_PROPERTY, FORM, WORKFLOW, IMPORT or EMAIL), whose results include ready-to-use filter fragments.

includeSampleMembers.description: Set true ONLY when the user wants to see examples of the matching records, not just how many there are. The result's sampleMembers then holds a few matching records by display name (a sample, never the whole audience). Leave false (the default) for a plain count; it skips an extra record lookup.

sampleProperties.description: Internal CRM property names of the object type to also return on each sampleMembers entry (e.g. 'industry', 'country'). Providing any implies includeSampleMembers. Leave empty to return sample members by name only.

countRecordsWithNoValue.description: Set true ONLY when the user asks how many records a != or NOT IN condition leaves out because they have no value for its property, e.g. "would including contacts with no company name make a difference?". The result's recordsWithNoValue then gives, per such condition, how many more records including them would add (0 means none). A condition on a date or inside an event filter can't include them and is not listed. Leave false (the default) otherwise; never set it on your own to decide whether to bring empty values up.

excludedSegmentIds.description: Optional: list IDs of segments whose members the segment will EXCLUDE, so the count leaves them out. Source them with SearchSegmentsQuery. When the user asks for a not-in-list FILTER instead, put the NOT IN_LIST condition in filterExpression and leave this empty.

excludedRecordIds.description: Optional: record IDs of the segment's own object type that the segment will EXCLUDE. At most 200.

excludeUnsubscribers.description: Set true when the segment will exclude unsubscribed contacts (default false). Contact segments only.

excludeNonMarketingContacts.description: Set true when the segment will exclude non-marketing contacts (default false). Contact segments only.

excludedEmailDomains.description: Optional: email domains whose contacts the segment will exclude. Contact segments only.

previewToken.description: Only when repeating a preview that failed with PREVIEW_STILL_RUNNING, including when the user later asks you to check it again: the previewToken from that error, copied exactly. Send it with the same objectType, filterExpression and exclusions to keep waiting on that same count instead of starting it over; the count keeps running in the background. Leave it empty (the default) for a new or changed preview; a token that doesn't match the query is ignored and the count starts from scratch.

anyOf.description:
Count how many records of an object type currently match a filter, without creating or saving
 anything, optionally leaving out the records the segment's exclusions would. Use it when the user
 asks how many records match, or wants a segment's size before it is saved; when the user simply
 asks for a segment, create it directly with CreateDynamicSegmentOperation.

operation.description: The read to perform. Set operation.type to SearchSegmentsQuery (find segments by name) or SearchFilterInputsQuery (resolve the ids used in filter expressions).

tools.name: tool_guidance
tools.title: Tool Guidance
tools.description:
<purpose>
              Retrieves guidance and usage instructions for a set of HubSpot tools.
            </purpose>

            <when_to_use>
              - If a tool's description isn't enough to commit to using it
              - To find if a tool's inputs or outputs have further semantic meaning
              - To learn understand if and how certain tools can work together
            </when_to_use>

            <how_to_call>
              Pass the names of the tools you want guidance for in `toolNames`
              (e.g. ["manage_crm_objects"]). Provide at least one tool name.
            </how_to_call>

toolNames.description: List of tool names to get usage instructions for
